'''Steven McManaman''' (born 11 February 1972) is an English former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[winger (association football)|winger]]. He is one of the most decorated English footballers to have played for a club abroad, with the [[UEFA]] website stating in 2012 that "of all England's footballing exports in the modern era, none was as successful as McManaman".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ross |first=Rory |date=10 September 2004 |title='I loved the life of a galactico's wife' |work=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3623692/I-loved-the-life-of-a-galacticos-wife.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=24 August 2009 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/3623692/I-loved-the-life-of-a-galacticos-wife.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name="uefa">{{Cite web |title=Ambassador:Steve McManaman |url=http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=1852347.html" |publisher=UEFA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140716044052/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=1852347.html |archive-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>

During his nine years at [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]],<ref name="lfcp">{{Cite web |title=Steve McManaman Official Liverpool Profile |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/history/past-players/steve-mcmanaman |access-date=16 August 2011 |publisher=Liverpool.com}}</ref> McManaman won the [[FA Cup]] and [[EFL Cup|League Cup]], while individually, he was the [[Premier League]]'s top assist provider for the [[1995-96 FA Premier League|1995–96 season]] and was named in the [[PFA Team of the Year]] for the [[1996–97 FA Premier League|1996–97 season]]. McManaman moved to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 1999,<ref name="ReferenceB">{{Cite news |date=14 March 1999 |title=Football: Houllier Set to Ditch Real Deal McManaman |work=Sunday Mirror |publisher=Thefreelibrary.com |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/FOOTBALL%3A+HOULLIER+SET+TO+DITCH+REAL+DEAL+McMANAMAN.-a060172883 |access-date=11 July 2014}}</ref> with the transfer becoming one of the most high-profile [[Bosman ruling|Bosman free transfers]] of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 July 2010 |title=Top Tens: Bosman transfers | Football Top Tens |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/35500.html |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=28 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928081518/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/35500.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Amongst his accomplishments with Madrid, he won [[La Liga]] and the [[UEFA Champions League]] twice, becoming the first English player to win the latter trophy with a non-English club, and later became the first English player to win it for the second time.<ref name="wing" /> An early [[Galácticos|''Galáctico'']], he won eight trophies and played in 11 cup finals in four years and made the semi-finals of the Champions League in each of his four years at the club. He went on to play two seasons at [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] before retiring in 2005.

Since his retirement, McManaman works as a co-commentator on [[ESPN]] and [[TNT Sports (United Kingdom)|TNT Sports (formerly BT Sport)]]'s football coverage, as well acting as a La Liga ambassador. He previously worked as a football [[pundit]] for [[Setanta Sports]].

==Early life==
Steven McManaman was born on 11 February 1972 in [[Bootle]], Lancashire<!--Bootle was in Lancashire until 1974-->.<ref name="Hugman"/> He grew up as an [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] supporter,<ref name="evertonian" /> with his boyhood heroes in football being the Everton players [[Bob Latchford]] and [[Duncan McKenzie]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2004 |title=Steve McManaman One on One |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/steve-mcmanaman-one-one |access-date=14 October 2020 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 2020 |title=Steve McManaman Boyhood Heroes (Interview) |url=https://twitter.com/5liveSport/status/1243626199764606982 |access-date=14 October 2020 |website=BBC 5 Live Radio on Twitter UK}}</ref> However, when Everton offered the player a two-year contract, after McManaman had made a name for himself at tournaments for school and around [[Merseyside]], McManaman's father rejected it in favour of a schoolboy contract and two-year apprenticeship offer from [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] (through scout Jim Aspinall and then-manager [[Kenny Dalglish]]).<ref name="evertonian">{{Cite news |last=Tongue |first=Steve |date=25 January 2009 |title=McManaman relishes spice of bitter rivalry - FA & League Cups, Football |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/mcmanaman-relishes-spice-of-bitter-rivalry-1515225.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/mcmanaman-relishes-spice-of-bitter-rivalry-1515225.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Death of scout who 'found' Anfield stars |work=Liverpool Echo |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/death-scout-who-found-anfield-3547829 |access-date=4 June 2019}}</ref> McManaman signed as a 16-year-old apprentice upon leaving school in 1988.<ref name="lfcp" /> As an apprentice, McManaman was under the mentorship of [[John Barnes]] and many regarded McManaman as a player who could potentially replace Barnes in the future.<ref name="liverpoolfc.tv">{{Cite web |date=5 September 2006 |title=100 PWSTK - No.22: Steve McManaman - Liverpool FC |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/100-pwstk-no-22-steve-mcmanaman |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110222180630/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/100-pwstk-no-22-steve-mcmanaman |archive-date=22 February 2011 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref> McManaman was said to be a natural [[sportsperson|athlete]]; having been a [[Cross country running|cross country]] champion at school level.<ref>{{Cite news |last=O'Hagan |first=Simon |date=30 July 1995 |title=Athletics: Robb comes on strong |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/athletics-robb-comes-on-strong-1593910.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 October 2018 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/athletics-robb-comes-on-strong-1593910.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Liverpool===
====1990–1993: Early years====
McManaman developed through the [[Liverpool F.C. Reserves and Academy|youth scheme at Liverpool]] and signed as a full professional on 19 February 1990 in what was to be [[Kenny Dalglish]]'s final full season as manager.<ref name="lfch">{{Cite web |title=Steve McManaman Profile |url=http://www.lfchistory.net/player_profile.asp?player_id=371 |access-date=24 August 2009 |publisher=LFCHistory.net}}</ref> On 15 December 1990, McManaman made his Liverpool debut under Dalglish as a substitute for [[Peter Beardsley]] in the [[Football League First Division]] in a 2–0 league win over [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] at [[Anfield]].<ref name="LFCHistory.net">{{Cite web |date=15 December 1990 |title=Liverpool 2-0 Sheffield United |url=http://www.lfchistory.net/viewgame.asp?game_id=1761&season_id=32 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070301085549/http://www.lfchistory.net/viewgame.asp?game_Id=1761&season_id=32 |archive-date=1 March 2007 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Lfchistory.net}}</ref> By the [[1991–92 Liverpool F.C. season|following season]], Dalglish had been replaced by [[Graeme Souness]] as manager.<ref name="liverpoolfc.tv" /> On 17 August 1991, he made his full debut in a 2–1 win over [[Oldham Athletic]]. This was a game in which ''[[The Guardian]]'' reported that McManaman "ran his legs into the ground" all day and assisted his mentor John Barnes in scoring the late winner by flicking on [[Mark Walters]]' cross.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 August 1991 |title=Barnes settles the passing groans |url=https://www.lfchistory.net/Images/newspapers/riley/19910817vOldham.pdf |access-date=28 April 2020 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> McManaman scored his first ever professional goal with a diving header four days later on 21 August 1991, in a 2–1 away defeat to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].{{citation needed|date=December 2024}}

The 19-year-old McManaman quickly became a regular first team player in the [[1991–92 Liverpool F.C. season|1991–92 season]], making 51 appearances in total in only his first full season. It was suggested that opportunities in the first team had come as a result of then manager Graeme Souness' decision to sell several ageing players.<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 October 1996 |title=Graeme He was also named the [[man of the match]], having set up the winning goal for [[Michael Thomas (footballer, born 1967)|Michael Thomas]],<ref name="lfch" /> despite being the youngest player on the pitch. McManaman's performances saw him described by [[Ian Rush]] as the most promising young player at Liverpool at the time.<ref name="lfch" />

====1993–1995: Success and first widespread fame====
Although McManaman had a couple of quieter seasons with the advent of the [[Premier League]], in which Liverpool initially struggled, he continued to develop a reputation as one of English football's two best emerging young wingers<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2017 |title=From McManaman to Mane: Liverpool's best wingers |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2017/05/01/from-mcmanaman-to-mane-liverpools-best-premier-league-right-wing/ |access-date=15 April 2020 |publisher=HITC Great Britain}}</ref> alongside [[Ryan Giggs]] of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref name="wing">{{Cite web |title=Steve McManaman Profile |url=http://www.givemefootball.com/player-profiles/steve-mcmanaman |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711100043/http://www.givemefootball.com/player-profiles/steve-mcmanaman |archive-date=11 July 2011 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Give Me Football}}</ref> A BBC article described the pair as able to "embarrass defences with their mazy runs, which too often lack the finishing touch they deserve".<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 July 2001 |title=Might of the midfielders |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/1433721.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hodgson |first=Guy |date=15 August 1997 |title=Football: Exuberant talent that so frustrates Anfield |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-exuberant-talent-that-so-frustrates-anfield-1245573.html}}</ref>

In the [[1993–94 Liverpool F.C. season|1993–94 season]], McManaman showed fine form with two goals against [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] and some assists including a spectacular run and assist against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. However, this form faltered following a drop in confidence after an incident with [[Bruce Grobbelaar]] towards the end of a [[Merseyside derby]], when the players exchanged blows after Grobelaar lambasted McManaman for a poor clearance<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010 |title=Football XIs of Clashes |publisher=ESPN |url=http://en.espn.co.uk/espn/sport/story/85317 |access-date=10 May 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> which led to a goal being conceded (an incident later named as one of the top five bust-ups between teammates in Premier League history).<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 December 2008 |title=Football's top five bust-ups |work=Blackpool Gazette |url=http://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sports-news/Football39s-top-five-bustups.4828149.jp |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref>

At the beginning of the [[1994–95 Liverpool F.C. season|1994–95 season]], McManaman signed a new million-pound contract, and was given a central, freer role<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 April 2017 |title=Football tactics: a brief history of three-man defences in English football |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/football-tactics-a-brief-history-three-man-defences-english-football |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref> by new manager [[Roy Evans]], who wanted to utilise McManaman's natural running and dribbling ability<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jiang |first=Allan |date=25 January 2012 |title=50 Greatest Dribblers in World Football History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1037524-50-greatest-dribblers-in-world-football-history |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> to drift all over the park. It proved a successful decision as McManaman began mesmerising defences with runs that were later to become hallmarks of the Liverpool side of the 1990s.<ref name="tifofootball1">{{Cite web |date=13 August 2018 |title=Steve McManaman: The Underrated icon of Liverpool's Spice Boys era |url=https://www.tifofootball.com/features/steve-mcmanaman-the-underrated-icon-of-liverpools-spice-boys-era/ |website=Tifo Football |access-date=15 March 2019 |archive-date=31 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331080903/https://www.tifofootball.com/features/steve-mcmanaman-the-underrated-icon-of-liverpools-spice-boys-era/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=16 February 2019 |title=Golden Goal: Steve McManaman for Liverpool v Celtic (1997) |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2019/feb/16/golden-goal-steve-mcmanaman-for-liverpool-v-celtic-1997 |access-date=1 April 2019 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> The 1994–95 season also proved to be a turning point for Liverpool after the lack of success during the previous two seasons. That season, he collected a [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] winner's medal after scoring twice in his side's 2–1 win over [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]; such was his performance that fans named it [[1995 Football League Cup Final|"The McManaman Final"]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steve McManaman – Liverpool F.C. |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/history/past-players/steve-mcmanaman |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Liverpool F.C.}}</ref> For his second [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] final appearance in succession he was awarded man of the match, earning the [[Alan Hardaker Trophy]] and a tribute from guest of honour, celebrated veteran winger [[Stanley Matthews]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Searl |first=Liz |date=3 April 1995 |title=They were two really great goals |work=The Independent McManaman before the final, saying: "I like the way you dribble,"<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Steinberg |first1=Jacob |last2=McCourt |first2=Ian |title=The Joy of Six: League Cup final goals |work=The |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[FourFourTwo]]'' magazine placed McManaman's performance in the final at number 87 on a list of the Top 100 best individual performances in all of modern By the end of [[1995–96 Liverpool F.C. season|1995–96]], McManaman was top of the Premier League goal assists chart with 25 assists over the season (15 in the Premier League),<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 November 2010 |title=Steve McManaman Joins ESPN as Soccer Analyst |url=http://espnmediazone.com/us/press-releases/2010/11/steve-mcmanaman-joins-espn-as-soccer-analyst/ |access-date=11 July 2014 |publisher=Espnmediazone.com}}</ref> including assists and top ratings in a [[Liverpool F.C. 4–3 Newcastle United F.C. (1996)|match against Newcastle United]] voted the best of the decade in the [[Premier League 10 Seasons Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stan-Ding Ovation!; Liverpool 4; Newcastle 3 |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/STAN-DING+OVATION!%3B+LIVERPOOL+4%3B+NEWCASTLE+3.-a061321367 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Thefreelibrary.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ten years and counting |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=264175&root=england&cc=5739 |access-date=17 December 2007 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=21 October 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071021090138/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=264175&root=england&cc=5739 |url-status=dead }}</ref> By now, McManaman was ranked as one of the finest midfielders in England and had developed a strong reputation on the European stage following [[UEFA Euro 1996]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dawson |first=Alan |date=15 January 2009 |title=Former Real Madrid Midfielder McManaman Believes Liverpool Can Win League Title |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1713/liverpool/2009/01/15/1062195/former-real-madrid-midfielder-mcmanaman-believes-liverpool-can-w |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090119002943/http://www.goal.com/en/news/1713/liverpool/2009/01/15/1062195/former-real-madrid-midfielder-mcmanaman-believes-liverpool-can-w |archive-date=19 January 2009 |access-date=11 July 2014 |website=Goal.com}}</ref> earning praise from many at the time including [[Kevin Keegan]], who said "there are few finer sights in world football than the sight of Steve McManaman running down the length of the pitch".<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-08-31 |title=SportMob – Best Players Ever in the History of Liverpool |work=SportMob |url=https://sportmob.com/en/article/874660-best-players-ever-in-the-history-of-liverpool |access-date=2023-03-03}}</ref>

====1995–1997: Consistency and success====
McManaman had also been noted for his versatility in his free role, switching from right to left wings, and his ability to play in central midfield, behind the front pair, or as a forward. McManaman was credited for making the free role that manager Evans gave him work,<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 August 1997 |title=Football: Exuberant talent that so frustrates Anfield |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-exuberant-talent-that-so-frustrates-anfield-1245573.html |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> with the result being that Liverpool were playing some of the most aesthetically pleasing attacking football at the time in England.<ref name="guardian.co.uk">{{Cite news |last=Smyth |first=Rob |date=15 February 2007 |title=On second thoughts ... ====1997–1998: Contract wrangles====
{{overly detailed|section|date=December 2024}}

In August 1997, Liverpool, having been unable to agree a new contract with McManaman and fearing that the player might leave on a [[Bosman ruling|Bosman free transfer]], finally accepted a £12 million bid for the player from [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]];<ref name="ReferenceA" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=20 January 1998 |title=Confusion surrounds Ł12m McManaman transfer |work=BBC News |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/49033.stm |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> Barcelona had previously tried (and failed) to sign McManaman twice before (after the [[1996 FA Cup final]] and after [[UEFA Euro 1996|Euro 96]]).<ref name="irishtimes1">{{Cite news |date=15 August 1997 |title=McManaman too costly for Barcelona |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/mcmanaman-too-costly-for-barcelona-1.97143 |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> The deal subsequently fell apart amidst recriminations about the player's remuneration demands and Barcelona's motives for the bid, being in negotiation with [[Brazil national football team|Brazilian]] superstar [[Rivaldo]] at the same time and snubbing McManaman when he travelled to Spain to meet them.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite news |last=Nixon |first=Alan |date=15 August 1997 |title=Barcelona move for McManaman |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/barcelona-move-for-mcmanaman-1245575.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/barcelona-move-for-mcmanaman-1245575.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> 

At its height, the transfer saga was dubbed by the ''[[International Herald Tribune]]'' (later acquired by ''[[The New York Times]]'') as one that ushered in a "new low in transfer trading tactics"; adding that McManaman was a pawn being "used" as the big clubs battled.<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 August 1997 |title=European Soccer : A New Low in Trading Tactics: Just Ask McManaman |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/18/sports/18iht-mac.t.html |access-date=18 July 2022}}</ref> By the end of the saga, Barcelona had signed Rivaldo after [[Bobby Robson]] changed his mind (he had earlier told LFC vice-chairman Peter Robinson that he wanted the player)<ref name="irishtimes1" /> and intervened and told [[Louis van Gaal]] that he decided McManaman was "a cosmetic player who would not score 18 goals a season for Barcelona",<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacKenzie |first=Niall |title=Bobby Robson interview |url=http://www.nufc.com/html/robson_independent.html |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=NUFC.com}}</ref> while McManaman himself, albeit expressing that he was surprised Liverpool were willing to sell him,<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 August 1997 |title=European Soccer : A New Low in Trading Tactics: Just Ask McManaman |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/18/sports/18iht-mac.t.html |access-date=11 December 2024}}</ref> stated that he had no desire to leave Liverpool and reiterated his former position in February 1997 - that he would not leave Liverpool no matter what unless the club ever decided to sell him, and with two years left on his contract was simply not in any rush to sign a new one - as cover for his waiting on the management and board to offer him the right contractual terms on a new deal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 August 2021|title=Steve McManaman: The Running Man |work=LFC History Net |url=https://www.lfchistory.net/articles/article/4612 |access-date=11 December 2024}}</ref> A subsequent bid of £11 million from [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moggi: Why Henry failed at Juve... | Football Italia |url=https://www.football-italia.net/144357/moggi-why-henry-failed-juve" |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190923061514/https://www.football-italia.net/144357/moggi-why-henry-failed-juve |archive-date=23 September 2019 |website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref> in November of the same year was rejected by both club and player.<ref name="espn.co.uk">{{Cite web |date=3 February 2011 |title=The leaving of Liverpool | Football First XIs |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/71786.html |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=11 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311180644/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/71786.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In early 1998, Barcelona returned with yet another bid for McManaman,<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 January 1998 |title=Confusion surrounds Ł12m McManaman transfer |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/49033.stm |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> and former [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] president Augusto César Lendoiro later added that Barcelona did not want to sign his former player Rivaldo and that they had (initially) wanted McManaman, and put it down to a "coincidence" that they pulled out and opted for Rivaldo instead,<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 October 2016 |title=El Barça no quería a Rivaldo, iba a por McManaman |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20161015/411024684026/rivaldo-lendoiro-depor-barca.html |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=Mundodeportivo.com}}</ref> with it being notable that the fact Barcelona came back again in 1998 (after having already signed Rivaldo five months earlier) had stood as evidence of that point. Nonetheless, McManaman and Liverpool turned them down once and for all for the last time.<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 January 1998 |title=McManaman move back on |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/mcmanaman-move-back-on-1.126346 |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>

McManaman had been named Liverpool stand-in captain at the start of the [[1997–98 Liverpool F.C. season|1997–98 season]],<ref name="lfcp" /><ref name="liverpoolfc.tv" /> but contract negotiations continued to flounder as the club could not match the sums available to McManaman if he left as a free agent at the end of the [[1998–99 Liverpool F.C. season|following campaign]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spice Boys Kop pounds 20m Offer; Double-yer-money bid to keep Macca and Robbie |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/SPICE+BOYS+KOP+pounds+20m+OFFER%3b+Double-yer-money+bid+to+keep+Macca...-a061110320 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Thefreelibrary.com}}</ref> Having been overlooked by [[Glenn Hoddle]] for the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] starting lineup, denounced in the English media as being greedy (due to the FC Barcelona fiasco) and bolstered by advice from the likes of fellow professionals [[Paul Ince]], [[Paul Gascoigne]], [[David Platt]] and [[Chris Waddle]],<ref name="madrid">{{Cite news |last=Nixon |first=Alan |date=30 January 1999 |title=Football: Macca in move to Real Madrid |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-macca-in-move-to-real-madrid-1077275.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-macca-in-move-to-real-madrid-1077275.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> McManaman publicly announced his desire to play abroad,<ref>{{Cite web |title=We're Real Keen on Macca; Spanish giants' shock |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/WE'RE+REAL+KEEN+ON+MACCA%3b+Spanish+giants'+shock.-a060629481 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Thefreelibrary.com}}</ref> explaining: "I have always said I would love the chance to play abroad and now that chance has come along. When you have a chance to join clubs who are involved in the Champions' League every season, you have to consider it...I'm sure everyone must see the logic in that."<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 December 1998 |title=Football: Macca: I'm totally committed |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/242672.stm |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref>

Numerous European clubs circled the soon-to-be free agent, with Juventus<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ross |first=Ian |title=McManaman eyes Juve and millions |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1998/nov/20/newsstory.sport}}</ref> again back in the fray amid huge media speculation, but [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] soon emerged in November through December 1998 as his most likely destination.<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 November 1998 |title=Race for Macca hots Up |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/217849.stm |access-date=24 August 2009}}</ref> In January 1999, it was reported that McManaman was talking to Real with the player reportedly offered £60,000 a week and nearly £2 million as a signing-on fee.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brand |first=Gerard |date=15 December 1995 |title=How the Bosman rule changed football - 20 years on |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/10100134/how-the-bosman-rule-changed-football-20-years-on |access-date=16 March 2019 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> On 30 January, McManaman passed a [[medical]] and signed an official pre-contract with the club which would make him the best-paid British footballer to date.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Lanson |title=Soccer News, January 30, 1999 |url=http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1999/01/30/phead.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629074730/http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1999/01/30/phead.htm |archive-date=29 June 2011 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Archives.tcm.ie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 1999 |title=McManaman's Spanish Jackpot |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/265954.stm |access-date=3 June 2017}}</ref> He declined to pose in a Real Madrid shirt at the contract signing event, out of respect for Liverpool's fans.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 1999 |title=Football: Macca in move to Real Madrid |work=The Independent |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-macca-in-move-to-real-madrid-1077275.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090706211639/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-macca-in-move-to-real-madrid-1077275.html |archive-date=6 July 2009}}</ref>

McManaman's image of being a contract rebel and [[mercenary]] at the time was also exacerbated by his involvement in a year-long dispute between 1997 and 1998 with [[Umbro]], his [[football boot]] sponsor. Umbro sued him for [[breach of contract]] for knowingly wearing [[Reebok]] branded boots in contravention of the deal, and deliberately "blacking out" their [[logo]] on his boots in protest.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 September 1997 |title=Star's footwork has Umbro fuming |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/star-s-footwork-has-umbro-fuming-1.105762}}</ref> McManaman argued that his contract was unenforceable and an unlawful [[restraint of trade]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Find articles |url=http://findarticles.com/p/news-articles/news-letter-belfast-northern-ireland-the/mi_7950/is_1997_Sept_12/steve-order-boot/ai_n35605187/?tag=rel.res1}}</ref> McManaman said that he was being exploited in that he was being held and tied to a boot deal he had signed back when he was a mere teenager. McManaman's agent during the 1990s, [[Simon Fuller]] and 19 Management<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 November 1997 |title=Henry remains loyal to Fuller in Spice Girls split |url=https://www.prweek.com/article/96050/henry-remains-loyal-fuller-spice-girls-split |website=PR Week}}</ref>—of which McManaman was his first football client<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thomas |first=David |date=2 November 2003 |title=Simon Fuller: Three-minute wonder |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/simon-fuller-three-minute-wonder-76180.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/simon-fuller-three-minute-wonder-76180.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 January 2007 |title=Becksploitation |url=https://www.marketingweek.com/becksploitation/ |website=Marketing Week}}</ref>—helped him negotiate a settlement.<ref>{{Cite news |date=8 November 1997 |title=Wannabe my manager? |work=BBC News |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/25520.stm}}</ref> The court initially ordered McManaman to fulfil his contract, plus an undertaking to pay Umbro's legal costs for launching [[contempt of court]] proceedings against him in 1997, which McManaman accepted and apologised for.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 September 1997 |title=ireland.com – The Irish Times – finance |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/finance/1997/0912/index.html |access-date=6 July 2011}} {{dead link|date=May 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> A year on, however, McManaman continued to dishonour the deal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 April 1999 |title=The entertainers |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/money/1999/apr/11/theyoungrich |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> He finally won an out-of-court [[Settlement (litigation)|settlement]] in October 1998, freeing him to negotiate with other companies for what he regarded as remuneration appropriate to his status.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 October 1998 |title=Umbro releases soccer star McManaman |url=https://www.marketingweek.com/1998/10/01/umbro-releases-soccer-star-mcmanaman/ |website=Marketing Week}}</ref>

====1998–1999: Final season at Liverpool====
{{overly detailed|section|date=December 2024}}

Having signed the pre-contract with Real Madrid, McManaman still had five months left on his contract at Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2010 |title=Gérard Houllier: The "Dynasty" Chapter |url=https://tomkinstimes.com/2010/09/gerard-houllier-the-dynasty-chapter/ |website=The Tomkins Times}}</ref> New manager [[Gérard Houllier]], who had replaced Roy Evans as full coach following the failure of their joint-managerial role that very season,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bascombe |first=Chris |date=1 October 2019 |title=Gerard Houllier exclusive interview: 'I'm surprised Liverpool fans are so nice to me' |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/10/01/gerard-houllier-exclusive-interview-surprised-liverpool-fans/ |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/10/01/gerard-houllier-exclusive-interview-surprised-liverpool-fans/ |archive-date=12 January |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3732837.stm}}</ref> and cavalier attitudes at the club,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Malam |first=Colin |date=24 November 2002 |title=Spice Boys are dancing to a new tune |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/leagues/premierleague/tottenham/3038405/Spice-Boys-are-dancing-to-a-new-tune.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 October 2008}}</ref> having told many players they were surplus to requirements (including [[Jason McAteer]], [[Phil Babb]], [[Rob Jones (footballer, born 1971)|Rob Jones]], [[Stig Inge Bjørnebye]], [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]] and [[Paul Ince]]), and where there were exits for seventeen other players who would leave the club in the next year ahead.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 May 2004 |title=Houllier pays the price for failure to live up to Liverpool's golden past |work=The Independent |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/may/17/match.sport3 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> ultimately stating that McManaman's departure was inevitable and the only chance of keeping him would [[Jamie Carragher]] defended McManaman in his autobiography, stating that at the time: "Despite being accused of greed, Macca also lost money to secure the move. I respect him for that."<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 March 2016 |title=Jamie Carragher: the perfect form of a true football fanatic |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2016/03/07/jamie-carragher-the-perfect-form-of-a-true-football-fanatic/ |website=Thesefootballtimes.co}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jamie Carragher: Born to play centre-half |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/announcements/258380-jamie-carragher-born-to-play-centre-half |website=Liverpool FC |date=29 March 2017 }}</ref> Another of McManaman's younger teammates, [[David Thompson (footballer, born 1977)|David Thompson]], also said (in an interview in 2019) that McManaman was the best player in that 1990s Liverpool team, but was playing as the playmaker of the side on a lower salary than even new foreign signings who came in on higher wage contracts at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 September 2019 |title=Undr the Cosh Episode #46 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nGuhQSUihks |access-date=29 January 2021 |website=Undr The Cosh Podcast}}</ref>

McManaman also stated that his decision to move abroad was something he had wanted to do for a long time and not for financial reasons alone,<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 May 2020 |title=Appreciating Steve McManaman: The genius who left after giving everything for Liverpool |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2020/05/appreciating-steve-mcmanaman-the-genius-who-left-after-giving-everything-for-liverpool/ |access-date=7 May 2020 |website=This is Anfield Liverpool News |location=Liverpool UK}}</ref> telling the magazine ''90 Minutes'' that it was about the allure of Real Madrid and [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]], [[Ferenc Puskás]] and Madrid's legacy, as well as the desire to test himself in the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 December 2016 |title=Steve McManaman Reveals Key Reason He Left Liverpool & Insists 'It Wasn't for Financial Reasons' |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/4233749-steve-mcmanaman-reveals-key-reason-he-left-liverpool-insists-it-wasn-t-for-financial-reasons |access-date=16 March 2019 |website=90 Minutes |archive-date=11 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161211115336/http://www.90min.com/posts/4233749-steve-mcmanaman-reveals-key-reason-he-left-liverpool-insists-it-wasn-t-for-financial-reasons? |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2021, McManaman finally shed new light on his decision to leave Liverpool back in 1999, stating that a combination of factors including being underappreciated at Liverpool – having not been offered the right contractual deal (as the club presumed on his staying on indefinitely simply because he was a local talent thus only sanctioning higher offers commensurate with his true value when they realised he would actually leave); and that the club were poor in communicating and handling his matters including selling him to FC Barcelona (without consulting him at all) – were all behind his decision back then. These were details which McManaman had never personally revealed publicly prior; and for over 20 years (arguably for confidentiality purposes and to protect the club's reputation).<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 March 2021 |title=Steve McManaman sheds new light on controversial free transfer to Real Madrid from Liverpool |work=Liverpool Echo |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/steve-mcmanaman-liverpool-real-madrid-20236173}}</ref>

At the time, in McManaman's final games for the club in the [[1998–99 Liverpool F.C. season|1998–99 season]], he began turning in mixed performances, with the media accusing him of playing out his final season in a "desultory manner".<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 November 2001 |title=Liverpool bids farewell to the last Spice Boy |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-bids-farewell-to-the-last-spice-boy-618630.html |access-date=6 July 2011}} {{dead link|date=August 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> His form dipped at times, largely due to a combination of injuries (his first recurrent achilles injuries for over five years having set in after years of playing constantly<ref name="independent1">{{Cite news |last=Walker |first=Paul |date=9 September 1998 |title=Football: McManaman injury worries Liverpool |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-injury-worries-liverpool-1197025.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-injury-worries-liverpool-1197025.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>)—where he had already missed an entire month from mid-November, only to return and reluctantly limp off the pitch (as captain)<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 December 1998 |title=Owen turns the tide for Reds |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1998/dec/28/match.sport1 |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> following a tackle by future Liverpool player [[Dietmar Hamann]] on his return game on Boxing Day (another compound injury that sidelined him for another month). Other factors for his loss of form included his later being restricted to substitute appearances (as Houllier wanted to cut the side's dependency on his gameplay and replace him,<ref name="ReferenceB" />) as well as suffering a loss of confidence in certain games where even the home fans turned against him over the contract debacle, with some labelling him a "traitor" and a [[Judas Iscariot|Judas]] figure.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pierson |first=Mark |date=6 March 1999 |title=McManaman Denies Fan Rift |work=The Independent |location=London |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-denies-fan-rift-1078784.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=24 August 2009 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-denies-fan-rift-1078784.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>

Nonetheless, Houllier also avoided dropping McManaman entirely from the squad and gave him the chance to play. Houllier stated: "Macca had decided to leave, that's why he didn't sign the year before. When I arrived it was his final year and I didn't want to punish him in any way for that, although I might have done with another player. It was not my fault Macca left. You never want your top players to leave the club. He went on a free under a new rule at the time and you have to live with that sometimes. I would have tried hard to sign him before he was able to leave, that's why I was fair to him. I wasn't going to prejudice the matter by not playing him; he played until the end of the season and I asked the fans to give him a great send off in the final game against Wimbledon."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houllier ready to learn from Macca memory |url=http://www.lfconline.co.uk/news/tmnw/houllier_ready_to_learn_from_macca_memory_134960/index.shtml |publisher=LFC Online}}</ref> McManaman himself also credited Houllier for his kindness during what ultimately was a difficult period,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Diallo |first=Raf |title=The Steve McManaman Special: Spice Boys, Galactico Life and Liverpool vs Barcelona |url=https://www.otbsports.com/sport/steve-mcmanaman-special-spice-boys-galactico-life-liverpool-vs-barcelona-855052 |website=Off The Ball}}</ref> adding: "...it was a difficult situation for the pair of us, so I've got nothing but respect for the way he acted."<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 August 2003 |title=Steve McManaman Interview |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/aug/29/newsstory.sport}}</ref>

''The Guardian'' reported on how divided the Liverpool fans were about McManaman's departure: "At the age of 27 McManaman is articulate enough to appeal to his public's elders, pretty enough to disrupt the thought patterns of the girls and good enough at his job to be regarded as a role model for the lads...on the face of it his crime is simply to be young, successful, in demand and wise enough to have surrounded himself with advisers who fully appreciate his true value. Before and during Saturday's game at Anfield he was subjected to some frightful abuse, accused by supporters of both teams of being a "greedy bastard"...It is wholly dependent upon your standpoint as to whether McManaman is a sporting trail-blazer enjoying the benefits of a free market or the very personification of the greed which many would argue has devalued football in recent times."<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 February 1999 |title=McManaman works his notice |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/feb/27/newsstory.sport9}}</ref> At the time, McManaman also suffered personal tragedy when his mother Irene died aged 50 after a long battle with cancer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 October 2003 |title=When my Mum was diagnosed with breast cancer at 44, it was such a shock |url=https://www.cheshire-live.co.uk/news/local-news/mum-diagnosed-breast-cancer-44-5306534 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715002402/http://www.chesterchronicle.co.uk/news/local-news/mum-diagnosed-breast-cancer-44-5306534 |archive-date=15 July 2014 |access-date=11 July 2014 |website=Ellesmere Port Pioneer}}</ref>

The combination of all these factors meant McManaman suffered a loss of form; however, McManaman managed to rally and pick up his play right at the end of that last campaign. McManaman scored a crucial goal away at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], set up a dramatic [[stoppage-time]] equaliser with a through-ball for Paul Ince to score in front of the Kop against Manchester United,<ref>{{Cite web |title=LFCTV Online :: Top Prem Goals: 41 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/video/100-collections/100-goals-premiership/5384-top-prem-goals-41 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. On 1 July 1999, after making 364 appearances and scoring 66 goals for Liverpool, McManaman transferred to [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] as [[Guus Hiddink]]'s last signing for the club. The transfer came before the dismissal of Hiddink and also came while the club was under president [[Lorenzo Sanz]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 January 1999 |title=McManaman's Spanish jackpot |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/265954.stm |access-date=7 March 2008}}</ref> Prior to the arrival of McManaman, Real Madrid was described as undergoing a management and debt crisis. Forward [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]] told the press that the [[dressing room]] was "a cesspit of lies, treachery and whispers" and commented that he felt "sorry for new players like Steve McManaman coming into the club".<ref name="Cesspit">{{Cite web |title=Football: Cesspit of Lies and Treachery; McManaman walking into a nightmare at Real Madrid, warn his new teammates |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3A+CESSPIT+OF+LIES+AND+TREACHERY%3B+McManaman+walking+into+a...-a060381417 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Thefreelibrary.com}}</ref> Raúl added that "[if] McManaman thinks he is coming to one of the world's top clubs then he has made a big mistake."<ref name="Cesspit"/> Previously, Real Madrid had appointed [[John Toshack]] as its new coach and had been obliged to sell influential players such as [[Predrag Mijatović]], [[Davor Šuker]] and [[Christian Panucci]] due to mounting debt, while Clarence Seedorf was later released shortly after McManaman arrived.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 December 1999 |title=Real Madrid continues decline from the European high of 1998 |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/real-madrid-continues-decline-from-the-european-high-of-1998.aspx?pageID=438&n=real-madrid-continues-decline-from-the-european-high-of-1998-1999-12-29 |access-date=12 July 2014 |website=Hurriyet Daily News}}</ref> 

McManaman's transfer saw him become only the second English player to ever play for the club after [[Laurie Cunningham]] had played for them in the 1980s. He became the first-ever player from the Premier League to move to play for Madrid<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoskin |first=Rob |date=25 August 2018 |title=Real Madrid have now signed 23 players from the Premier League - how have they fared? |url=https://www.givemesport.com/1378622-real-madrid-have-now-signed-23-players-from-the-premier-league-how-have-they-fared |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=GiveMeSport}}</ref> and was also the most high-profile English footballer to move for Spanish football since [[Gary Lineker]] had moved to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] from [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 1986. When McManaman first arrived, he admitted an initial struggle with loneliness,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=George |date=27 March 2020 |title=Steve McManaman on pressure, loneliness and what links Liverpool and Real Madrid |work=Liverpool Echo |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-real-madrid-comparison-mcmanaman-17998335 |access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> and spoke at the time of retired former Liverpool player [[Michael Robinson (footballer)|Michael Robinson]] being his mentor.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 May 2002 |title=From teenage flop at City to Spanish 'Des', the opinionated life of Robinson |work=The Independent UK |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/from-teenage-flop-at-city-to-spanish-des-the-opinionated-life-of-robinson-9234540.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |agency=Press Association |date=28 April 2020 |title=Michael Robinson: The Liverpool fan who found his home in Spain |work=Evening Express UK |url=https://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/sport/michael-robinson-the-liverpool-fan-who-found-his-home-in-spain/ |access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1999 |title=Michael Robinson: Leaving Liverpool for Spain |url=https://www.lfchistory.net/Articles/Article/3873 |access-date=28 April 2020 |website=LFC History Net}}</ref> Robinson had likewise moved to Spain to play football and |access-date=28 April 2020 |website=Thinking Heads Celebrity Management }}{{Dead link|date=April 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Following a successful pre-season with the Madrid team in Switzerland<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 July 1999 |title=Steve McManaman of Real Madrid in Lausanne |url=https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/steve-mcmanaman-of-real-madrid-in-lausanne-during-a-pre-news-photo/1222278 |access-date=28 April 2020 |website=Getty Images News}}</ref> and Italy, McManaman and his teammates returned to Spain. McManaman proved immediately to be popular with Real Madrid's supporters at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] after scoring three times and creating several goals in his first few pre-season games for ''Los Merengues''.<ref name="wright" /> On 22 August 1999, McManaman made his debut for Real Madrid in a 2–1 win over [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] at the [[ONO Estadi|Son Moix]] stadium in [[Mallorca]], where he assisted [[Fernando Morientes]] in scoring a stoppage-time equaliser and thus enabling Madrid to go on to win 2–1 with seconds remaining.<ref name="vice">{{Cite web |date=13 June 2017 |title=Steve McManaman, The First British Galactico |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/steve-mcmanaman-the-first-british-galactico/ |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=Vice.com}}</ref>

On 29 August 1999, McManaman scored his first goal for the club on his home debut in a 4–1 victory over [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] at home. From December 1999 to January 2000, McManaman and the Madrid team took part in the controversial inaugural [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship|FIFA Club World Championships]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]], where McManaman missed a stoppage-time chance to win a game against [[Club Necaxa|Necaxa]] and then also missed the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] that would have sent Madrid into third place.<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 January 2000 |title=Mexican penalty kings depose Real |work=BBC News |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/special_report/1999/12/99/world_club_championship/604240.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> Following this tournament, McManaman and the team returned to Spain and established themselves as a strong European side under new coach [[Vicente del Bosque]], who had replaced John Toshack in November. McManaman's form in the run-in for the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] title saw him receive several man of the match awards,<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 March 2018 |title=Steve McManaman, Real Madrid's Sixth Man |url=https://www.tifofootball.com/features/mcmanaman-real-madrid/ |access-date=11 March 2019 |website=Tifo Football |archive-date=1 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401042757/https://www.tifofootball.com/features/mcmanaman-real-madrid/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> forming a productive midfield partnership with [[Fernando Redondo]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 April 2000 |title=Real Madrid 0 – 0 Man Utd |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/apr/04/championsleague.sport3 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> as Madrid beat title defenders Manchester United<ref>{{Cite news |date=5 April 2000 |title=Bosnich passes Spanish Inquisition |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/apr/05/championsleague.sport2 |access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] to reach the [[2000 UEFA Champions League final|final]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 May 2000 |title=Real Madrid 2 – 0 Bayern Munich |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/03/championsleague.sport |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> On 24 May 2000 in the [[2000 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]] at the [[Stade de France]], [[Paris]], McManaman arguably experienced his finest moment as a professional footballer, scoring a spectacular volley in a 3–0 victory over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. His performance on the greatest of club football stages saw him hailed as the man of the match by the English press,<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 May 2000 |title=McManaman the matador toys with Valencia |work=The Guardian |location=London |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/25/championsleague.sport1 |access-date=24 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lacey |first=David |date=25 May 2000 |title=Real reveal Spain's upper class |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/may/25/championsleague.sport2 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> a view endorsed by his Madrid teammate [[Iván Helguera]].<ref name="independent.co.uk">{{Cite news |date=13 August 2000 |title=McManaman smiles all the way to the bank |work=The Independent |location=London |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/internationals/mcmanaman-smiles-all-the-way-to-the-bank-696673.html |url-status=live |access-date=24 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090914032423/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/internationals/mcmanaman-smiles-all-the-way-to-the-bank-696673.html |archive-date=14 September 2009}}</ref> McManaman's part in Madrid's eighth European Cup win also saw him become the first English player ever to win Europe's premier club competition with a foreign club.<ref name="tifofootball1" /><ref name="vice" />

====2000–01: Fortitude in Madrid====
Despite the Champions League final performance and having established himself as a valuable player in his first year in Madrid (including being listed alongside [[Fernando Redondo]] in Real Madrid's technical director [[Pirri]]'s end of season official report as one of the two "untouchables" around whom the team should be built for the coming campaign),<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 August 2000 |title=England lift for McManaman |work=Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/4769280/England-lift-for-McManaman.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=3 September 2019 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/4769280/England-lift-for-McManaman.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> the arrival of a new club president in [[Florentino Pérez]], closely followed by former Barcelona superstar midfielder [[Luís Figo]] in a club-record transfer, saw the club forced to sell several key players to reduce debt. season]] and would be sold.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 August 2000 |title=Figo not the major arrival |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/891286.stm |access-date=6 July
