|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/mcmanamans-fall-from-grace-isnt-unusual/article769228/ |access-date=20 April 2020}}</ref> and remove his $4.5 million salary from the wage bill.<ref name="forbes.com" /> McManaman, however, with an iron-clad contract until 2004, declined to leave<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 August 2000 |title=McManaman stands his ground |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/4765247/McManaman-stands-his-ground.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=20 April 2020 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/4765247/McManaman-stands-his-ground.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and instead stated his determination to win back his place in the team.<ref name="independent.co.uk" />

McManaman was left out of Real Madrid's squad for the [[2000 UEFA Super Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title= McManaman in Chelsea talks |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/aug/25/newsstory.sport2 |website=The Guardian |date= 25 August 2000 |access-date=3 June 2023 |last1= Taylor |first1= Chris }}</ref> Real Madrid subsequently accepted first an [£11 million bid from [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and then a £12 million bid for McManaman from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Taylor |first=Chris |date=25 August 2000 |title=McManaman in Chelsea talks |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/aug/25/newsstory.sport2 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> that included the exchange of [[Tore André Flo]], in the summer of 2000, both of which the player rejected. A [[Sky Sports]] report in August 2000 also stated that eight other clubs were vying for his signature at the time, including Manchester United, [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] and [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 December 2010 |title=Eight in for McManaman |work=Sky Sports |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,,11667_2189740,00+en-USS_01DBC.html |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> Alex Ferguson declared his admiration for McManaman by arranging a contingent to convince him to sign.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Davies |first=Christopher |date=15 August 2000 |title=United join chase for McManaman |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/4766777/United-join-chase-for-McManaman.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/4766777/United-join-chase-for-McManaman.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> McManaman, however, said he wanted to succeed in Spain. His stance was rewarded when Real relented after a Spanish poll in ''[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]'' showed 90% of the fans wanted the club to keep McManaman, while [[Míchel Salgado]] complained to the management about the way McManaman was treated after McManaman turned down again another transfer attempt, this time to [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]], who came in with an £8 million offer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cass |first=Bob |date=3 September 2000 |title=McManaman looks to Lazio escape route |url=http://www.espnfc.com/europe/news/2000/0903/20000903laziomacca.html |access-date=12 July 2014 |website=espnfc.co |publisher=ESPN FC}}</ref> In September of that year, several Real Madrid first-team stars were reported as having taken up a dressing room revolt collectively for McManaman and went to speak to Del Bosque directly. ''[[The Guardian]]'' reported that a ''Marca'' article had one prominent player stating: "We cannot stand by while this is happening. What happened to Redondo happened — well in the end Fernando had a good offer — but McManaman, what has Macca done to deserve the treatment he is getting from the manager?...[McManaman has been] treated with disrespect and is being humiliated—for no reason at all."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ingle |first=Sean |date=1 September 2000 |title=Real players plot dressing room revolt over Macca |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/sep/01/newsstory.sport8}}</ref>

An ''[[El País]]'' report in early September 2000 reported Del Bosque as being sympathetic (albeit the fact that his hands were tied) concerning McManaman with Del Bosque saying: "I expected the audience to be affectionate with McManaman because he is a player very dear here. We will try to unite Real Madrid through the game although there are sectors that think more about those who are not."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Torres |first=Diego |date=6 September 2000 |title=Redondo and McManaman get the biggest ovation from the Bernabéu |work=El Pais |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2000/09/06/deportes/968191202_850215.html}}</ref> McManaman meanwhile was adamant that even if the situation to get him to leave was created around him, no one from the club's hierarchy ever told him to leave to his face,<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 April 2019 |title=Steve McManaman: "Soy muy 'florentinista', pero creo que este verano se equivocó" |url=http://m.libertaddigital.com/deportes/liga/2019/04/03/steve-mcmanaman-soy-muy-florentinista-pero-creo-que-este-verano-se-equivoco-1276635939/ |website=M.libertaddigital.com}}</ref> with the Spanish press even expressing the strange paradox of the whole situation by revealing that Del Bosque had actually rated McManaman highly and was quoted as saying: "Steve es el que entiende mejor cómo quiero que juguemos" ("Steve is the player in the team who best understands how I want us to play").<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bengoechea |first=Jesús |date=3 May 2019 |title=McManaman: "Soy muy florentinista, aunque Este verano se equivocó" |work=La Galerna |url=https://www.lagalerna.com/galerna-entrevista/mcmanaman-la-galerna/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=McManaman: "Soy muy florentinista, aunque este verano se equivocĂł" |url=https://www.lagalerna.com/galerna-entrevista/mcmanaman-la-galerna/ |website=La Galerna|date=3 April 2019 }}</ref>

Real Madrid's hierarchy's change toward McManaman began when Del Bosque gave him his first appearance of the 2000–01 season as a substitute in a 3–3 draw against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] in mid-September.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Findon |first=Ben |date=18 September 2000 |title=European Round-up: McManaman back in Real favour |work=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/4771602/European-Round-up-McManaman-back-in-Real-favour.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=24 May 2010 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/4771602/European-Round-up-McManaman-back-in-Real-favour.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> McManaman reportedly won over the manager by October and managed to feature in two-thirds of the club's matches, becoming a first-team regular for the remainder of the campaign—holding the unique distinction of being described as the only top-class football player from England playing overseas at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuper |first=Simon |date=July 2000 |title=European goal |url=http://www.prospect-magazine.co.uk/printarticle.php?id=3638 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707004638/http://www.prospect-magazine.co.uk/printarticle.php?id=3638 |archive-date=7 July 2009 |access-date=12 July 2014 |publisher=Prospect Magazine}}</ref> McManaman was also primarily deployed as a left-winger in this season (with Figo on the right), with the press noting that "the 'telepathy' McManaman and [[Roberto Carlos]] displayed down Madrid's left flank flummoxed almost every team they played."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Return of the MACCA |url=http://www.irishnews.com/sport/2013/12/19/news/return-of-the-macca-78886/ |access-date=1 April 2019 |website=The Irish News|date=19 December 2013 }}</ref> McManaman shone in this second season as Madrid advanced to the semi-finals of the Champions League (only to lose to eventual winners Bayern Munich), and won their 28th [[La Liga]] crown by a seven-point margin over the previous season's champions, Deportivo La Coruña; the club's first La Liga title in four years,<ref name="wright">{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=James |date=14 July 2003 |title=Englishmen Abroad: Steve McManaman |url=http://www.thefa.com/Features/EnglishDomestic/Postings/2003/07/56755.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20040530101314/http://www.thefa.com/Features/EnglishDomestic/Postings/2003/07/56755.htm |archive-date=30 May 2004 |access-date=7 March 2008 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> with McManaman recording eight assists,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hemingway |first=Rob |date=2 February 2022 |title=How Macca and Becks Rocked Europe with Real Madrid |url=https://www.planetfootball.com/nostalgia/real-madrid-english-players-david-beckham-steve-mcmanaman-champions-league/ |access-date=12 February 2022 |publisher=Planet Football}}</ref> and making 42 appearances in all competitions that year despite missing the first two months of the season.<ref name="vice" />

====2001–02: Second Champions League====
Eventually, the Board, including Florentino Pérez, relented, declaring that a "man like that would always have a place in my club", adding that "McManaman is in now in the team because his behaviour has been in accordance with the true values of the club".<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 January 2001 |title=Real Madrid president says Figo born to play for club |url=http://www.rediff.com/sports/2001/jan/28real.htm |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=rediff.com}}</ref> [[Johan Cruyff]] described McManaman at the time as the most useful player in the ''Galácticos'' because he was ''el socio del todos''<ref>{{Cite news |title=Golden Goal: Steve McManaman for Liverpool v Celtic (1997) |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2019/feb/16/golden-goal-steve-mcmanaman-for-liverpool-v-celtic-1997 |access-date=11 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 2018 |title=The Big Interview: Steve McManaman - El Socio del Todos |url=https://grahamhunter.tv/steve-mcmanaman-el-socio-del-todos-2/ |access-date=7 May 2020 |website=The Graham Hunter Podcast}}</ref> ("everyone's best partner on the pitch").<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=30 December 2010 |title=Ronaldo, Zinedine Zidane lead Real Madrid's Team of Decade – Sid Lowe |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/sid_lowe/12/28/realmadrid.alltimeXI/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110102103510/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/sid_lowe/12/28/realmadrid.alltimeXI/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 January 2011 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> McManaman's partnership role functioned as one of a "perpetual motion style (that) moved defenders out of position and allowed the (Galatico) superstars to flourish".<ref>{{Cite news |date=5 November 2018 |title=Liverpool's bittersweet thrill of Steve McManaman thriving at Real Madrid |work=Planet Football |url=https://www.planetfootball.com/nostalgia/liverpools-bittersweet-thrill-of-steve-mcmanaman-thriving-at-real-madrid/ |access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref>

A further honour was also extended on the pitch by the club in December 2002, whereas part of Madrid's Centenary Celebrations, McManaman was made the first Englishman to captain Real Madrid in a game against a [[FIFA]] World XI, to the applause of the [[ultras]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Torres |first=Diego |date=5 September 2000 |title=Redondo y McManaman se llevan la mayor ovación del Bernabéu |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2000/09/06/deportes/968191202_850215.html |via=elpais.com}}</ref> with whom he had always been a cult favourite,<ref name="vice" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 January 2019 |title=British players that made their mark in Europe |url=https://themalestrom.com/sport/brits-abroad-footballers-that-made-their-mark-europe/ |access-date=16 March 2019 |website=The Malestrom}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 September 2017 |title=Liverpool's McManaman was a rare English success abroad with Real Madrid |url=https://www.theversed.com/44962/mcmanaman-liverpool-real-madrid-transfer-success/#.kTyyzCvYD1 |access-date=16 March 2019 |website=Theversed.com}}</ref> and where the group is sometimes also known as the Ultra South (or "Ultrasurs").<ref>{{Cite web |last=Internet |first=Unidad Editorial |title=A Bernabéu without 'Ultras' - MARCA.com (English version) |url=https://www.marca.com/2013/12/02/en/football/real_madrid/1386010116.html |website=MARCA}}</ref>

Another great moment in the white of Madrid took place in the 2002 UEFA Champions League semi-final against Barcelona at the [[Camp Nou]] on 23 April 2002. In this match of huge proportions, due to ''[[El Clásico]]'' being a massive game in its own right, but also the fact that it was a Champions League semi-final, McManaman appeared as a second-half substitute to score a critical goal in second-half stoppage time to secure a 2–0 first-leg advantage, chipping over goalkeeper [[Roberto Bonano]] after being played in by [[Flávio Conceição]], after Zidane had scored the first goal on 55 minutes. After the game [[Jorge Valdano]] added: "McManaman? McManaman is connected to everybody. A football match is a game of little societies and McManaman is a member of them all."<ref name="auto">{{Cite news |date=16 March 2002 |title=McManaman, no one asked about him |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/mar/16/sport.comment |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> This notable victory, Real's first at the Camp Nou since 1993, helped secure their place in the [[2002 UEFA Champions League final|final of the 2002 Champions League]] at [[Hampden Park]], [[Glasgow]], where McManaman came on as a replacement for Figo on the hour mark – and thereby ensuring his second Champions League winners' medal, after Madrid secured a 2–1 victory over German team [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]].<ref name="wright" />

====2002–03: Final season====
McManaman was used as a late substitute for games at the start of the campaign and after scoring a goal and assisting in a couple of new signing Ronaldo's goals<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=7 October 2002 |title=Ronaldo scores on his first date |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/oct/07/europeanfootball.sport2 |access-date=28 August 2019 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> he was given surprise starts. In one of his starts, he scored a brace against [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] in the Champions League. McManaman also started in a game in 2003 in which Madrid were beaten 4–3 at [[Old Trafford]] against Manchester United in the Champions' League, even as Ronaldo hit a hat-trick.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wallace |first=Sam |date=24 April 2003 |title=McManaman has the last laugh |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2400232/McManaman-has-the-last-laugh.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2400232/McManaman-has-the-last-laugh.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Nonetheless, after only playing 21 games of which he started only nine times, and making a meagre 15 appearances in [[La Liga]], questions constantly arose throughout the season about McManaman's ability and reasons for staying in Spain considering his diminished role, lack of first-team action and international attention. Suggestions that McManaman had "sold out" for money and had grown indifferent and lackadaisical to his football were rampant in the British Press, while Ian Farrell, writing in ''[[When Saturday Comes]]'', described the British press as suffering from "a selective media amnesia over McManaman's time in Spain".<ref>{{Cite web |title=When Saturday Comes – The Half Decent Football Magazine – Return of the Mac |url=http://www.wsc.co.uk/content/view/2350/29/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716153649/http://www.wsc.co.uk/content/view/2350/29/ |archive-date=16 July 2011 |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Wsc.co.uk}}</ref> Nonetheless, McManaman managed to pick up a second [[La Liga]] medal for the year and was in the squad that won the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] in Japan.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}}

At the start of the [[2003–04 Real Madrid CF season|2003–04 pre-season]], the signing of fellow Englishman [[David Beckham]] proved the last straw in eventually forcing McManaman down the pecking order at Real Madrid. McManaman remained with the club for its full pre-season, even after coach [[Vicente del Bosque]] was dismissed a day after having won the club's latest La Liga title,<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 June 2003 |title=Players and fans shocked by Del Bosque sacking |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/players-and-fans-shocked-by-del-bosque-sacking-541795.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100922124201/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/players-and-fans-shocked-by-del-bosque-sacking-541795.html |archive-date=22 September 2010}}</ref> but in the close season, and the arrival of [[Carlos Queiroz]] as the new coach, McManaman was released by the club after helping Beckham with the language and to settle in,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Taylor |first=Louise |title=Inscrutable Beckham charms China |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/aug/02/sport.comment |access-date=11 March 2019}}</ref> despite Beckham's pleas with the management for McManaman to remain.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 July 2003 |title=Figo takes Beckham under his wing |work=Irish Examiner |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/soccer/figo-takes-beckham-under-his-wing-107433.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=25 July 2003 |title=Beckham stays silent on first day at the office |work=The Independent |url=http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/beckham-stays-silent-on-first-day-at-the-office-97550.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/beckham-stays-silent-on-first-day-at-the-office-97550.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>

===Manchester City===
====2003–2004: Arrival and impressive performances====
In 2003–04, along with Madrid teammates [[Claude Makélélé]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 August 2003 |title=Chelsea line up Makelele to take spending over £100m |newspaper=The Times |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/chelsea-line-up-makelele-to-take-spending-over-pound100m-n7tbp3v7r2f}}</ref> [[Fernando Hierro]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 February 2010 |title=Real Madrid: Fernando Hierro nuovo vice di Ancelotti |url=https://www.football-magazine.it/real-madrid-fernando-hierro-nuovo-vice-di-ancelotti/ |publisher=Football-magazine.it}}</ref> and Fernando Morientes,<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 January 2005 |title=Owen signing was final straw for Morientes |work=The Irish Examiner |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-30184773.html}}</ref> McManaman headed back to the [[Premier League]]. Initially reported to be joining [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] or [[Everton F.C.|Everton]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 August 2003 |title=Moyes hopes to bring McManaman home |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/moyes-hopes-to-bring-mcmanaman-home-537312.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090909100823/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/moyes-hopes-to-bring-mcmanaman-home-537312.html |archive-date=9 September 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 July 2003 |title=Garcia lets McManaman's Arsenal secret out – ABC News (Australian Broadcasting Corporation) |url=http://abc.gov.au/news/stories/2003/07/18/904860.htm |access-date=6 July 2011 |publisher=Abc.gov.au |newspaper=ABC News}}</ref> McManaman eventually decided to join long-time admirer [[Kevin Keegan]] on 30 August at [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 April 2020 |title=How Manchester City's Masters Football Team Would Look in 2020 |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/6593785-how-manchester-city-s-masters-football-team-would-look-in-2020 |website=90min.com}}</ref> resulting in a reunion with several ex-colleagues including [[Robbie Fowler]], [[Nicolas Anelka]], and later, [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]], prompting the media to state that Keegan was "reuniting the Spice Boys".<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 August 2003 |title=McManaman joins Man City |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/3193141.stm |access-date=7 March 2008}}</ref>

McManaman made his debut on 14 September 2003 in a 4–1 win over Aston Villa at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]], and quickly showed good early form<ref>{{Cite news |last=Edworthy |first=Sarah |date=15 September 2003 |title=McManaman's unreal debut |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2421463/McManamans-unreal-debut.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2421463/McManamans-unreal-debut.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> with the club starting with a run of wins<ref name="search.japantimes.co.jp">{{Cite web |date=3 October 2003 |title=England could use experience, skill of McManaman in lineup |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2003/10/03/soccer/england-could-use-experience-skill-of-mcmanaman-in-lineup/ |access-date=12 July 2014 |website=The Japan Times Online}}</ref> and progressing in the [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]], with McManaman hailed by Keegan to great hype, but by [[Christmas]] that year, results had fallen, the team languished<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Chris |date=22 July 2004 |title=Keegan throws down the gauntlet |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/keegan-throws-down-the-gauntlet-1116223 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714141808/http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/keegan-throws-down-the-gauntlet-1116223 |archive-date=14 July 2014 |access-date=12 July 2014 |website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> and ended the season, well out of European contention, and McManaman injured again. By 2004–05, McManaman's time at City was ultimately deemed a disappointment and he was increasingly vilified by City fans,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moss |first=Stephen |date=21 September 2004 |title=Spice Boy grows up |work=The Guardian |location=London |url=https://www.theguardian.com/g2/story/0,,1308935,00.html |access-date=7 March 2008}}</ref> who later jeered him off the pitch<ref>{{Cite news |title=The Big Interview: Steve McManaman |date=3 September 2023 |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/the-big-interview-steve-mcmanaman-6q8scz9lr2r |via=www.thetimes.co.uk}}</ref> following a draw with [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=City release be end of the line for McManaman |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/City+release+may+be+end+of+the+line+for+McManaman.-a0124090360 }}{{Dead link|date=April 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

====2004–2005: Loss of form and departure====
On the pitch, a combination of niggling injuries (including a long-term achilles problem not dissipating<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goss |first=Patrick |title=McManaman to leave City |work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11679/2335856/mcmanaman-to-leave-city |access-date=11 March 2019 }}</ref>) and the rise of an in-form and up-and-coming [[Shaun Wright-Phillips]] saw him lose his preferred right midfield position. When McManaman did play, he failed to rediscover his old form and speed, only occasionally demonstrating the ability he had shown in his earlier career.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moss |first=Stephen |date=21 September 2004 |title=Spice Boy grows up |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/sep/21/sport.comment3 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> Part of the problem stemmed from the fact that to find a role at Madrid he had changed his playing style,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Palmer |first=Kevin |date=29 May 2020 |title=Steve McManaman: I had to turn games for Liverpool; there were seven at Real |work=Planet Football |url=https://www.planetfootball.com/in-depth/steve-mcmanaman-i-had-to-turn-games-for-liverpool-there-were-seven-at-real/ |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> cutting down on the flair play (as Madrid had a surfeit of flair players) and instead focusing on being a holding player and making short, simple passes of the ball in central midfield, where he was known for his one-touch passing and ability to never give the ball away.<ref name="wright" />

In February 2004, McManaman was criticised by Alex Ferguson after an [[2004–05 FA Cup|FA Cup]] [[Manchester derby]] at Old Trafford for "intimidating [[Gary Neville]]" to get him sent off in a [[headbutt]] incident, adding a derogatory comment that he had no idea what other role McManaman had in the game [and possibly for Manchester City].<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 February 2004 |title=Ferguson fumes over Neville's card |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2373114/Ferguson-fumes-over-Nevilles-card.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2373114/Ferguson-fumes-over-Nevilles-card.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

|url=http://www.as.com/actualidad/articulo/escandalo-sexual-mcmanaman-fowler/dasftb/20031111dasdai_43/Tes |access-date=7 March 2004}}</ref> that appeared in the ''[[News of the World]]'' following a failed attempt by the pair to gain an injunction to prevent publication, costing them £50,000 in addition to making the case look like an invariable admission of guilt.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Greer |access-date=7 March 2004 |authorlink=Germaine Greer}}</ref> The court case came soon after football's "[[Group sex|roasting]]" and [[rape]] allegations at [[Chelsea, London|Chelsea]] earlier that |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/keegan-rage-at-citys-spice-boys-6962166.html |url-status=live |website=Thisislondon.co.uk}}</ref>

In 2004, McManaman was linked to the [[New York Red Bulls|MetroStars]], who confirmed that the club were interested in him. However, they eventually decided to relinquish their bid stating that "[[MLS]] clubs were keen to lose the reputation that top stars only arrive to play in America for a final swansong in their careers".<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 June 2011 |title=MetroStars give up on Macca |work=Sky Sports |url=http://origin.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11679_2293701,00.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716083304/http://origin.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11679_2293701,00.html |archive-date=16 July 2011}}</ref> McManaman played for City for only two seasons and following [[Kevin Keegan]]'s resignation in March 2005, never played another game for the club. Keegan's replacement, [[Stuart Pearce]], released McManaman on a free transfer on 20 May.<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 June 2011 |title=McManaman to leave City |website=Sky Sports |url=http://origin.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11679_2335856,00.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716083417/http://origin.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11679_2335856,00.html |archive-date=16 July 2011}}</ref>

===Retirement===
McManaman retired from his playing career after being released by Manchester City in 2005.<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 May 2005 |title=Manchester City let McManaman go |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/4565335.stm}}</ref> He ended his career across all his three clubs with a total of 566 appearances, scoring 80 goals. In early 2006, McManaman nearly came out of retirement to sign for the [[Hong Kong Rangers FC|Hong Kong Rangers]], a club owned by an admirer of his football, [[Carson Yeung]], but the deal fell through due to McManaman's recurrent injuries which scuppered his fitness test.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 December 2006 |title=McManaman rules out making return |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/6171473.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref>

==International career==
===Summary===
McManaman is sometimes described as an enigma at international level for [[England national football team|England]]. Excluding [[Terry Venables]] and [[Kevin Keegan]], every England manager decided to utilise McManaman's talents sparingly. McManaman was capped 37 times for England and scored three goals. England lost only three times in the games that he played;<ref name="thefa.com" /> these included the [[UEFA Euro 1996]] penalty shootout defeat to Germany at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] in 1996, and the opening day defeat against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] at [[UEFA Euro 2000]]. Over his 11 years as an England international, McManaman played in tournaments such as UEFA Euro 1996 and the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]]. UEFA Euro 2000, held in the Netherlands and Belgium, was McManaman's last major tournament for England, despite pressure from the press, fans and teammates, including [[Zinedine Zidane]], to include him in the final squad for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Webster |first=Rupert |title=Macca: Left Side or Left Home? |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11835/2236098/macca-left-side-or-left-home |website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

===1990–1993: England U21===
McManaman made history by becoming the first player without first-team experience to play for the [[England national under-21 football team|England under-21]] team, being handed a debut call-up by [[Lawrie McMenemy]] against [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales]] at [[Prenton Park|Tranmere]] in October 1990, two months before he debuted for the Liverpool first-team. McMenemy commented that he had seen "more fat on a chip" referring to McManaman's [[Underweight|skinny]] physique.<ref name="wing" /> In February 1993, McManaman captained the under-21 team for the first time against [[San Marino national under-21 football team|San Marino]] and scored the last goal in a 6–0 win.{{citation needed|date=December 2024}}

===1993–1997: Senior breakthrough and UEFA Euro 1996===
[[Terry Venables]] gave McManaman his full debut on 16 November 1994 in an international friendly with [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]], McManaman coming on as a replacement for [[Rob Lee]]. By 1995, McManaman was accused of struggling to repeat his fine club form with his country, drawing comparisons to his mentor at [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], John Barnes. However, he managed to string together a series of match winning performances for his country at [[UEFA Euro 1996]], earning praise from [[Pelé]], who according to the [[BBC]] touted him as the tournament's best player<ref>{{Cite news |title=Steve McManaman resembling Inspector Gadget | England 4 Holland 1 at Euro 96 - where are they now? |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/03/29/england-4-holland-1-at-euro-96---where-are-they-now/steve-mcmanaman-resembling-inspector-gadget/ |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 October 2018 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/03/29/england-4-holland-1-at-euro-96---where-are-they-now/steve-mcmanaman-resembling-inspector-gadget/ |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and said he was the player he "was most impressed" by;<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 June 2000 |title=Pele Backs England for Glory |publisher=BBC |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/england/781303.stm}}</ref> before going on to say that he was "one of the best players in Europe" and could be the "best in the world"<ref name="thefa.com">{{Cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/England/SeniorTeam/Archive/?&i=4811&t=m&t=pf |title=Archive |publisher=The Football Association |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090121075735/http://www.thefa.com/England/SeniorTeam/Archive/ |archive-date=21 January 2009 |access-date=14 January 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=6 June 2000 |title=Pele praises McManaman and Larsson |work=BBC News |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/779965.stm |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> (at the time).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steve McManaman |url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/bios/steve-mcmanaman/ |access-date=29 December 2022}}</ref>

The tournament began with a game against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in which McManaman swapped wings interchangeably with [[Darren Anderton]] and created "all kinds of problems on the left".<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 1996 |title=England 1 Switzerland 1 Match Report |url=http://linguasport.com/futbol/internacional/eurocopa/1996_ENGLAND_FS.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220115017/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/internacional/eurocopa/1996_ENGLAND_FS.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=20 December 2014 |access-date=6 May 2020 |website=Lingua Sport}}</ref> McManaman and [[Teddy Sheringham]], and later [[Paul Gascoigne]], were then substituted in order to save them for the next game when England were leading 1–0 with 15 minutes remaining. This decision led to an immediate outpouring of unhappiness and jeering from the crowd at Wembley.{{citation needed|date=February 2026}} Following this, England switched to a defensive 4–5–1 formation which saw them concede a late penalty and end up drawing the game 1–1.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 May 2020 |title=Euro 96, the complete history – part two: The opening ceremony and England vs Switzerland |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/euro-96-england-switzerland-complete-history-alan-shearer-wembley |access-date=12 May 2020 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 July 2016 |title=The cultural resonance of Euro 96 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/in-bed-with-maradona/2016/jul/06/euro-96-england-germany-music-sport-tony-blair |access-date=6 May 2020 |website=The Guardian}}</ref>

McManaman was noted by pundits for his "mesmerising dribbling skills" and willingness to take players on. [[Gary McAllister]] later claimed in the BBC's post-match analysis of England's next game against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] that it was Venables' change of England's tactics at half-time to switch to a five-man midfield and introduce [[Jamie Redknapp]] into the midfield that allowed McManaman the freedom to open up the Scottish defence. McAllister believed that this changed the game, with Redknapp and McManaman unlocking the openings which led to [[Gary Neville]]'s cross for [[Alan Shearer]]'s headed opener in the 2–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 June 2012 |title=Rewind to Euro '96, when England's Gareth Southgate went from a piece of history to Pizza Hut |url=http://en.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/154038.html |publisher=ESPN |access-date=28 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Football news, features and statistics | FourFourTwo |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/ |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

Despite having a quiet first half in England's next game against the Netherlands, McManaman was involved in all of England's first three goals against the opposition: firstly, he supplied the inside cut final pass for Ince who was subsequently brought down in the area for a penalty which Shearer scored from;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=19 June 1996 |title=England's night of rapture |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/englands-night-of-rapture-1337711.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/englands-night-of-rapture-1337711.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |website=The Independent}}</ref> secondly, his cross to Anderton was deflected for a corner kick from which Sheringham headed the second goal; and finally, his quick one-two with Gascoigne led to England's third and Shearer's second in the game which ended up in a [[UEFA Euro 1996 Group A#Netherlands vs England|4–1]] victory. This was believed to be a landmark result at the time.<ref>{{cite web |last=Massarella  |first=Louis  |date=10 June 2016 |title=FourFourTwo's 50 Most Memorable Euros Goals: 9. Alan Shearer, ENGLAND v Holland, 1996 |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/fourfourtwos-50-most-memorable-euros-goals-9-alan-shearer-england-v-holland-1996 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

Frequently man-marked in the quarter-final against [[Spain national football team|Spain]], McManaman burst back into the latter part of the semi-final against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and in the final moments of extra-time nearly assisted Darren Anderton in scoring a late winner. However, Anderton's shot from McManaman's cross hit the post and the ball bounced back into the hands of the goalkeeper.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering Euro 96: Jamie Redknapp, Darren Anderton, Stuart Pearce and Steve Howey |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/18804/10295641/remembering-euro-96-jamie-redknapp-darren-anderton-stuart-pearce-and-steve-howey |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> Together with teammates Gascoigne, Shearer and [[David Seaman]], McManaman was listed in the official Team of the Tournament, as well as shortlisted behind eventual winner, [[Jürgen Klinsmann]], for the Most Valuable Player award.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smyth |first=Rob |date=4 July 2007 |title=On Second Thoughts: Rob Smyth says Euro 96 wasn't how it is usually remembered |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/jul/04/1 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref>

===1997–1999: Tactical Conundrums and 1998 FIFA World Cup===
{{overly detailed|section|date=December 2024}}

McManaman, however, failed to win over new England coach [[Glenn Hoddle]] despite being in excellent club form in the years Hoddle was in charge,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=29 September 1997 |title=Football: Why Hoddle cannot turn a blind eye to McManaman |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-why-hoddle-cannot-turn-a-blind-eye-to-mcmanaman-1241856.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-why-hoddle-cannot-turn-a-blind-eye-to-mcmanaman-1241856.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> raising questions about either his effort, his attitude, or his relationship with the manager, with some sections of the British press even lobbying Hoddle to pick McManaman. [[Roy Evans]] (McManaman's coach at the time) also voiced his opinion regarding his England situation to ''The Independent'' before the [[1998 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 2|1998 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]], saying: "There is not a player like him in England. I think he's fantastic, he's certainly a great asset from our point of view...We don't pick the England team but I see him as the perfect linkman in the international team. But that's only our opinion. We believe he is top, top quality."<ref name="independent1" />

Hoddle stated in interviews that he wanted McManaman to take up that very licence to be the bridge between [[David Beckham]] and [[Paul Gascoigne]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fox |first=Norman |date=11 May 1997 |title=Football: An invitation for McManaman |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-an-invitation-for-mcmanaman-1260892.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-an-invitation-for-mcmanaman-1260892.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> and often spoke highly of McManaman's ability, but said that McManaman's best position was "floating" dangerously and it was hard to fit him into a system to suit the team<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ridley |first=Ian |date=2 February 1997 |title=McManaman a dangerous floater |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/mcmanaman-a-dangerous-floater-1276392.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/mcmanaman-a-dangerous-floater-1276392.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> and so he often selected [[Paul Merson]] and the rising Beckham instead. When McManaman (and [[Robbie Fowler]]) opted out of [[Le Tournoi]] in 1997 to choose to undergo non-urgent medical operations ahead of international duty, it was noted that this reportedly lost them their team spots as Hoddle though angered at losing them, found a winning team in their absence, and this made it even harder for McManaman to regain his place later.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=30 August 1997 |title=Football: Hoddle happy to call up 'victimised' Wright |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-hoddle-happy-to-call-up-victimised-wright-1248075.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-hoddle-happy-to-call-up-victimised-wright-1248075.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>

McManaman (and Fowler) were also reported at the time to have been marginalised by Hoddle for not embracing Hoddle's employment of a "faith healer" and mystic named Eileen Drewery, who had been brought in by Hoddle to do psychiatric, vague spiritual or psychological interactions with the players because Hoddle had said she helped him in his career in the past.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Guru whose faith failed to help Hoddle keep his job |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/1999/feb/03/3" |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513014512/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/1999/feb/03/3 |archive-date=13 May 2019 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> McManaman and Fowler allegedly poked fun at Drewery by asking her "if she knew the winner of the 3.15 at Wincanton so they could put a bet on", while McManaman was reported as saying that 'Hoddle's training camps were "like joining the [[Moonies]]."'<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2018 |title=The Hod Complex: England and the 1998 World Cup |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/world-cup/2018/the-hod-complex-england-and-the-1998-world-cup_sto6795833/story.shtml |publisher=Eurosport}}</ref> McManaman's England colleague, Gary Neville conceded Hoddle's methods were regarded as bizarre<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 February 1999 |title=Hoddle sacked |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/270194.stm}}</ref> and included other devices such as 'heart touching', getting staff to walk around the pitch anti-clockwise to create 'positive energy' and the use of legal sporting injections,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chronnell |first=Paul |title=Gary Neville reveals bizarre England methods under Glenn Hoddle |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/aug/21/gary-neville-england-glenn-hoddle |access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref> with McManaman and Fowler allegedly not the only ones who were unable to accept or fit in with Hoddle's training system, and McManaman accusing Hoddle of running things like a cult; favouring those players who were willing to acquiesce to him.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Goodchild |first1=Sophie |last2=Kossoff |first2=Julian |date=31 January 1999 |title=Glenn Hoddle: The trouble with Glenn |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/glenn-hoddle-the-trouble-with-glenn-1077340.html |url-status=dead |access-date=3 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120113000919/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/glenn-hoddle-the-trouble-with-glenn-1077340.html |archive-date=13 January 2012}}</ref>

McManaman played a total of four full games out of six starts in his seven appearances under Hoddle,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=24 March 1998 |title=Football: McManaman must destroy the myth |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-must-destroy-the-myth-1152186.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-must-destroy-the-myth-1152186.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> including only one appearance at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] against [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]], as a substitute for [[Paul Scholes]]. Despite only playing 17 minutes, the press described McManaman's performance: "In 17 minutes did enough to demonstrate that his dainty dribbling could yet be influential against miserly defences. Still gives ball away too much."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brenkley |first=Stephen |date=28 June 1998 |title=Football: England's man-for-man marking |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-englands-man-for-man-marking-1168227.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=23 September 2019 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-englands-man-for-man-marking-1168227.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref>

In Beckham's eponymous autobiography in 2013, he revealed that on the day after [[1998 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Argentina vs England|the defeat]] to [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the 1998 World Cup, when he felt all alone and distraught back at the team hotel, it was McManaman (along with [[Terry Byrne]] and the England team's masseur, Steve Slattery), who stayed behind to accompany him and play [[snooker]] with him late into the night; in order to help take his mind off the fallout of that defeat (having been made the culprit by some sections of the media and fans for getting sent off during that match).<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FX18AQAAQBAJ&pg=PA41 |title=David Beckham Biography |date=31 October 2013 |publisher=Headline Book Publishing |isbn=978-0-7553-6592-0 |page=41 |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref>

Before McManaman joined Madrid, Spanish media outlets like ''El País'', eager to make sense of why Madrid were insisting on signing McManaman when he had not even featured much in the last World Cup, concluded that the only rationale to explain McManaman's non-selection by Hoddle must have been because McManaman was known as a free role-playing playmaker, and was "difficult to classify. He needs the point of freedom...not provided in the English team" and that he was therefore by implication, difficult to place into Hoddle's system.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Segurola |first=Santiago |date=16 November 1998 |title=El expreso de Anfield |language=es |trans-title=The Anfield express |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/diario/1998/11/16/deportes/911170819_850215.html |access-date=28 August 2019}}</ref> According to Ian Ridley of the Irish Independent Newspaper, "...it was significant that the best ball-carrier in the country, Steve McManaman, prospered under Venables but languished under Hoddle."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ridley |first=Ian |date= 9 February 1999 |title="Venables: Still the Players Choice"|work=Irish Independent |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/venables-still-the-players-choice/26258038.html |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>

When interviewed by ''FourFourTwo'', McManaman stated, "I think I probably least enjoyed my time when Glenn Hoddle was the manager. But I wouldn't say he was necessarily the worst. He had his ways of training and ways of acting and all managers have different ways of doing things; it's the same with club managers. Sometimes when you join up with England and you don't play as often as you did under a certain other manager—then you'll think it's terrible. I loved going to play with England. For instance, I did get to go to the World Cup even though I only played for 17 minutes. That kind of experience leaves an indelible mark on your mind. So I don't really think of it in terms of "worst"; but going to the World Cup and not playing much was a big thing for me, really, and that was under Glenn, of course."<ref name="fourfourtwo.com">{{Cite web |date=5 October 2004 |title=Steve McManaman – One-On-One – Interviews |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/interviews/one-on-one/341/article.aspx |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref> Hoddle also arranged for McManaman to meet a disabled fan (and thus fulfil his lifelong wish of meeting McManaman) while the fan was on the verge of death, in 1997,{{Citation needed|date=October 2018}} though the story only broke a year after Hoddle had been dismissed from the England job.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Arlidge |first=John |title=Hoddle's future in doubt after disabled slur |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/jan/30/newsstory.sport7 |access-date=28 October 2018}}</ref>

===1999–2001: Reinstatement and UEFA Euro 2000===
After [[Kevin Keegan]] was appointed as England manager, he quickly reinstated McManaman to the England [[starting lineup]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 2000 |title=Macca playing the Goat |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/apr/23/newsstory.sport |access-date=13 March 2020}}</ref> further adding that he thought McManaman was one of the best midfielders in Europe.<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 May 2000 |title=Real prove genuine article |newspaper=The Irish Times |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/real-prove-genuine-article-1.274962 |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> John Barnes spoke about McManaman in his autobiography in 1999 as "probably the greatest individual talent in English football and has to be presented the correct way",<ref>{{Cite news |date=10 October 1999 |title=John Barnes's karma kicks in: 'Wrong to sack Hoddle' |work=The Observer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/oct/10/newsstory.sport14 |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> and Keegan gave several interviews in 1999 backing up that point; adding that he was finding out how best to utilise McManaman.

Keegan eventually decided on deploying McManaman on the left-wing on several occasions in 1999<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=28 April 1999 |title=Football: McManaman free to prove point |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-free-to-prove-point-1090196.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-free-to-prove-point-1090196.html |archive-date=25 May 2022}}</ref> and under Keegan, McManaman finally broke his international goal scoring duck when he scored twice on 4 September 1999 in the 6–0 [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying Group 5|Euro 2000 qualifier]] victory over [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]], again, at Wembley. Keegan took McManaman's new career at Madrid as a basis to reinstate his confidence in him, and handed him a coveted free role ahead of [[UEFA Euro 2000]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 June 2000 |title=McManaman given free role |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/england/787372.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> stating that "in the past we compromised him ... but [following McManaman's UEFA Champions League success], we said 'we'll fit in with you, you've earned that chance'.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lappin |first=Tom |title=McManaman keeps feet on the ground |url=http://sport.scotsman.com/top-stories/McManaman-keeps-feet-on-the.2233952.jp |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=Sport.scotsman.com}}</ref> At the time, even former coach [[Glenn Hoddle]] chimed in with support for this decision, adding that though he feared teams would not give McManaman (and the team) the space he thrived on at the tournament, he believed that finding a way to deploy McManaman effectively in a special system was difficult "but it can be done."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoddle |first=Glenn |author-link=Glenn Hoddle |title=The Glenn Hoddle Column: Macca is flying but will need special system |url=http://www.espnfc.com/euro2000/columns/20000528feathoddle2.html |access-date=10 May 2020 |website=ESPN Soccernet}} {{dead link|date=September 2020}}</ref>

McManaman's free role for England was shortlived as he played only once in Euro 2000, scoring the last of his three England goals in the opening game against Portugal, where he put England 2–0 ahead (with a volley off [[David Beckham]]'s cross) after only 18 minutes, but got injured early in the second half whilst making a tackle on [[Rui Costa]] in midfield,<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 June 2000 |title=McManaman and Adams to miss Germany game | Football | the Guardian |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/jun/13/euro2000.sport13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218024221/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/jun/13/euro2000.sport13 |archive-date=18 February 2019}}</ref> forcing a tactical switch.<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 June 2000 |title=England crushed in five-goal classic |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/788135.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> England ended up losing the game 3–2,<ref>{{Cite news |title=England crushed in five-goal classic |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/788135.stm}}</ref> and McManaman would remain injured and miss the rest of the tournament as England exited at the group stage. McManaman never played another competitive match for Keegan again as he was ruled out with injury<ref>{{Cite news |title=England fear for McManaman |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1999/sep/30/newsstory.sport2}}</ref> for Keegan's last couple of games before his shock resignation<ref>{{Cite news |title=Keegan quits after England lose to Germany |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1369368/Keegan-quits-after-England-lose-to-Germany.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1369368/Keegan-quits-after-England-lose-to-Germany.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> from the England job in October 2000.

===Post 2001: Omission from squad===
{{overly detailed|section|date=December 2024}}

The last of McManaman's caps came in 2001 when new coach [[Sven-Göran Eriksson]] utilised him for England's first few games in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 9|2002 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] — including a game back at [[Anfield]] against [[Finland national football team|Finland]] (where McManaman admitted before the game that he had yet to achieve significant success with England and was hungry to prove himself<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 March 2001 |title=Macca Promises England Rebirth |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2002/1235124.stm |access-date=14 October 2019}}</ref>) and where he would go on to set up [[David Beckham]]'s winner.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 March 2001 |title=Clockwatch: England v. Finland |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/3001668/Clockwatch-England-v.-Finland.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/3001668/Clockwatch-England-v.-Finland.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

By late 2001, however, after coming on as a substitute when England beat [[Germany national football team|Germany]] [[Germany 1–5 England (2001)|5–1]] in the [[Olympiastadion (Munich)|Olympiastadion]], McManaman put in a display against [[Albania national football team|Albania]] of "such apathy" according to ''[[The Guardian]]'' that the paradox of McManaman was stated as follows: "If McManaman is thought of at all in England now, it is as a man for whom exclusion beckons. Given his status at Real, England's World Cup squad should be comfortably within his grasp but McManaman, befitting someone who patrols the flanks, is drifting towards the periphery of Sven-Goran Eriksson's radar. The question is not whether McManaman, 30 a month ago, has the ability to force his way back into the centre of Eriksson's considerations but whether he has the will. In England's World Cup qualifier against Albania at St James' Park last September, four days after Munich, he made a fleeting appearance of such apparent apathy that even he was taken aback, never mind Eriksson."<ref name="auto" /> That performance saw McManaman banished from Eriksson's team,<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 September 2003 |title=Return of the Macca |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=276173&root=england&cc=3436 |website=Soccernet |publisher=ESPN |access-date=22 June 2008 |archive-date=7 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707071228/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=276173&root=england&cc=3436 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as that was his penultimate game; making just one substitute appearance after that in the critical qualifier against [[Greece national football team|Greece]] in 2001.

McManaman stated in his biography that he was struggling at the time working out if Eriksson rated him, saying that although he could see reasons why the coach dropped him (Eriksson picked [[Emile Heskey]] ahead of McManaman to start the Greece game<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 June 2001 |title=Buoyant England see off Greece |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2002/1372822.stm |access-date=28 October 2018}}</ref> and only brought McManaman on when England were still 2–1 down with 15 minutes to go), he (McManaman) wondered: "[I didn't understand it]; if he didn't rate me, why would he bring me on against Greece [when we were losing]?" This prompted some media commentators such as [[Brian Reade]] to suggest that it was McManaman's attitude, mentality or pride<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reade |first=Brian |date=20 April 2002 |title=Macca: From a Floppy-fringed genius to Flop on the fringes |work=The Mirror |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/macca-from-a-floppy-fringed-genius-to-flop-on-the-fringes-535671 |access-date=12 May 2020 |authorlink=Brian Reade}}</ref> that Eriksson did not like and was the reason for his drop.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lawton |first=Matt |date=5 October 2001 |title=Bar-room stories cheer Greeks and leave Rehhagel seeking punchline |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/3014133/Bar-room-stories-cheer-Greeks-and-leave-Rehhagel-seeking-punchline.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=28 October 2018 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/3014133/Bar-room-stories-cheer-Greeks-and-leave-Rehhagel-seeking-punchline.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Later that year, McManaman "chose not to play" in the game against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] by calling [[The Football Association|the FA]] to have himself dropped from the squad,<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 November 2001 |title=McManaman 'chose not to play' |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/1640672.stm |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> before assistant coach at the time, [[Tord Grip]] said: "McManaman has never really played well for England".<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 December 2002 |title=McManaman out in cold |work=BBC Sport |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/england/2537597.stm}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=10 December 2002 |title=ESPN.com Soccernet Column by Phil Ball: Macca para Inglaterra |url=http://www.espnfc.com/columns/2002/1210/20021210featball.html |website=ESPN FC}}</ref> Following that, McManaman was not selected for another England squad.

By early 2002, Eriksson apparently left a message on McManaman's [[answering machine]] to inform him that he was not going to be in the final World Cup squad.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Edworthy |first=Sarah |date=7 May 2002 |title=England need McManaman for world stage |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/england/3027320/England-need-McManaman-for-world-stage.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707215027/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/international/england/3027320/England-need-McManaman-for-world-stage.html |archive-date=7 July 2009}}</ref> Despite the pleas of McManaman's Real Madrid teammates [[Zinedine Zidane]], [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 April 2002 |title=Raul questions Macca Omission |work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/2237557/raul-questions-macca-omission |access-date=11 September 2020}}</ref> and [[Fernando Hierro]] for McManaman's case, McManaman said he never heard from or met Eriksson again. Zidane went on to state England had made a mistake and described McManaman as one of the highest quality players he ever played with.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 April 2002 |title=Eriksson must select McManaman, says Zidane |url=http://www.rediff.com/sports/2002/apr/26wc2.htm |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=Rediff.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=26 April 2002 |title=Zidane backs McManaman for World Cup |work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/2236062/zidane-backs-macca-for-world-cup |access-date=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Support for McManaman also came before the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] in the British media, after Sky Sports published an article based on [[Opta Sports|Opta]] statistics, revealing that despite a poor goalscoring record, McManaman had, in fact, an 88% dribbling completion rate (having embarked on a run every 17 minutes), and an 84% pass completion rate, all three of which were higher by over 15% than any English midfield Premiership player at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Webster |first=Rupert |title=Is Macca Good Enough for England? |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11667/2204555/is-macca-good-enough-for-england |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> However, the same statistics also cast light on a different kind of dilemma for Eriksson after it was revealed that: "...For Real Madrid, he (McManaman) completed 83% of his passes and while that figure only fell to 82% in the Champions League it dropped to 73% when he was wearing an England shirt. For Madrid, he completed 85% of his dribbles and runs in the league and 83% in Europe but under Eriksson for England he only managed to keep the ball 63% of the time...the general belief for this drop in form when playing for England is simple. At Liverpool and Real Madrid, McManaman was in a side that liked to hold possession and move the ball about, pull teams apart and create spaces to move into. England tend to be more direct and less patient with their football and keep a more rigid formation. While at Anfield he was given pretty much a free-role and at Real Madrid the players all move about as they pass teams into submission, but England stick to a 4-4-2 formation and that does not suit him."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pomroy |first=Matt |date=30 May 2002 |title=McManaman: Stats Show Why Sven Said No |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/2237232/mcmanaman-stats-show-why-sven-said-no |access-date=28 January 2022 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

==Player profile==
===Style of play===
A hard-working, versatile and technically gifted player, McManaman was usually deployed as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]], or occasionally as a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]]. His preferred position, however, was that of a more offensive and creative [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rowe |first=James |date=10 May 2020 |title=David Thompson on the Institution that is Liverpool FC and Generational Talent McManaman |work=World Football Index |url=https://worldfootballindex.com/2020/05/david-thompson-on-the-institution-that-is-liverpool-fc-generational-talent-mcmanaman/ |access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> an uncommon position in the Premier League throughout his career. McManaman was a quick, strong, creative, and energetic player with  tremendous [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] ability as well as accurate passing and [[Cross (association football)|crossing]] ability with either foot. This allowed him to create chances and provide assists for teammates. He was often criticised, however, for his inability to score many goals, although he would later improve upon this element of his game during the peak of his career.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Football: McManaman changes perceptions |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-changes-perceptions-1277870.html |access-date=18 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=La Liga Legends – Steve McManaman |url=http://www.footballislife.co.uk/football/la-liga-legends-steve-mcmanaman |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218222122/http://www.footballislife.co.uk/football/la-liga-legends-steve-mcmanaman |archive-date=18 December 2014 |access-date=18 December 2014}}</ref> In October 2016, McManaman was nominated for the award of England's best dribbler of all time, an award eventually won by [[Stanley Matthews]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Norgrove |first=Oliver |date=7 October 2016 |title=Stanley Matthews out in front in voting for England's best dribbler |newspaper=The Times |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/stanley-matthews-out-in-front-in-voting-for-englands-best-dribbler-wbwmjbp03 |access-date=23 June 2019}}</ref>

Though McManaman was occasionally criticised for scoring too few goals, he did make up for this with a formidable rate of assists for the likes of [[Robbie Fowler]] – with whom he was described as having an almost "telepathic" understanding<ref>{{cite web |title=Made for each other: The most prolific partners |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/623528 |publisher=Premier League |date=14 February 2018}}</ref> – and, later [[Michael Owen]], with Owen saying that "Liverpool at the time was built around McManaman"<ref>{{Cite news |title=Liverpool v Manchester United: Anfield club remain a work in progress under Brendan Rodgers |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/10277248/Liverpool-v-Manchester-United-Anfield-club-remain-a-work-in-progress-under-Brendan-Rodgers.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 October 2018 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/10277248/Liverpool-v-Manchester-United-Anfield-club-remain-a-work-in-progress-under-Brendan-Rodgers.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and was an average team whenever McManaman was not on form.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Owen |first=Michael |date=20 June 2010 |title=World Cup 2010: Wayne Rooney can get back in the goals to spark Three Lions into life |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup-2010/teams/england/7840656/World-Cup-2010-Wayne-Rooney-can-get-back-in-the-goals-to-spark-Three-Lions-into-life.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 June 2010 |authorlink=Michael Owen}}</ref> Additionally, McManaman's role as the creative playmaking lynchpin in the side meant that scoring statistics alone were not often believed ===Reception===
====Liverpool====
McManaman is generally believed to be very popular in Liverpool. ===="Spice Boys"====
As the fame of McManaman and his teammates increased, [[Tabloid (newspaper format)|tabloid]] newspaper stories of [[lad culture]] excesses emerged and this, fused with underachievement on the pitch, brought criticism in the media. Defeat to Alex Ferguson's Manchester United in three title races (from [[1995–96 Liverpool F.C. season|1995–96]] through [[1996–97 Liverpool F.C. season|1996–97]]) including the [[1996 FA Cup final]], a game where the Liverpool team arrived to inspect the pitch wearing cream coloured [[Armani]] suits- intensified the criticism.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilkerson |first=Ian |date=16 February 2006 |title=FA Cup flashback |work=BBC News |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/4694012.stm |access-date=24 May 2010}}</ref> McManaman and other teammates were reported to have cashed in on their newfound fame as stars of the nascent Premier League, to live a high life involving [[groupies]], [[nightclub|clubbing]] and other "high jinks". Modelling contracts and deals with fashion labels like [[Topman|Top Man]], [[Hugo Boss]] and Armani culminated in their collective nickname, the "[[Spice Boys (footballers)|Spice Boys]]".<ref>{{Cite news |date=17 January 2004 |title=James joins Spice Boys for quiet reunion – Premier League, Football |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/james-joins-spice-boys-for-quiet-reunion-573424.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090909114704/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/james-joins-spice-boys-for-quiet-reunion-573424.html |archive-date=9 September 2009}}</ref>

The situation was further aggravated by stories of McManaman and best friend [[Robbie Fowler]]'s lifestyles off the pitch following an interview with the magazine ''[[Loaded (magazine)|Loaded]]'', which depicted the duo as [[hedonists]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 September 2004 |title=Spice Boy grows up |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/sep/21/sport.comment3 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> and 'scally' characters, as well as stories about McManaman and Fowler's lack of decorum and disruptive influence in the dressing room.<ref name="guardian.co.uk" /> McManaman responded by joining ''[[The Times]]'' to write a weekly column, becoming the first footballer of his generation to do so.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Moore |first=Glenn |date=10 February 1997 |title=Football: McManaman changes perceptions |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-mcmanaman-changes-perceptions-1277870.html |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> McManaman's columns were known for articulating opinions on matters from a player's perspective,<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 1997 |title=Football: McManaman's World |work=The Times (Archived) |url=https://archive.org/stream/NewsUK1997UKEnglish/Oct%2011%201997%2C%20The%20Times%2C%20%2366018%2C%20UK%20%28en%29_djvu.txt |access-date=10 May 2020}}</ref> and in one particular column, discussed the issue of how the Bosman ruling impacted the future of the English game with "cut-price imports" that threatened local development, while also proposing the increasing of odds for smaller teams to beat big clubs by having the League Cup reduced to a single leg affair, thus enabling players to be better rested as well.<ref>{{Cite news |date=23 September 1996 |title=McManaman: Cut Price Imports Threaten Domestic Game |work=The Times (Archived) |url=https://archive.org/stream/NewsUK1996UKEnglish/Sep%2023%201996%2C%20The%20Times%2C%20%2365691%2C%20UK%20%28en%29_djvu.txt |access-date=10 May 2020}}</ref> By 1998, following the success of his well-regarded columns, he also began writing monthly pieces for ''Esquire'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Segurola |first=Santiago |date=November ====Under the ''Galácticos'' policy====
While he was seen as an early Galáctico in his time at Real Madrid, McManaman increasingly saw his playing time reduced each year as the club further initiated their ''[[Galácticos]]'' policy, with new high-profile players like [[Luís Figo]], [[David Beckham]], [[Zinedine Zidane]] and [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] arriving each year and often starting more matches than him. At the time, however, McManaman was known for his dogged determination to stay positive for the club's cause, even if it meant he had less playing time.<ref name="tft">{{Cite news |last=Townsend |first=Jon |date=2 April 2020 |title=Steve McManaman at Real Madrid: The most successful English player to head overseas |work=These Football Times |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2020/04/02/steve-mcmanaman-at-real-madrid-the-most-successful-english-player-to-head-overseas/ |access-date=14 April 2020}}</ref> In 2002, McManaman turned down a transfer to [[Inter Milan]] at the time when he was made available for exchange as part of Ronaldo's signing.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Davies |first=Christopher |date=3 September 2002 |title=McManaman has no interest in Inter move |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/leagues/premierleague/3033838/McManaman-has-no-interest-in-Inter-move.html |url-status=dead |access-date=6 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090707215033/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/leagues/premierleague/3033838/McManaman-has-no-interest-in-Inter-move.html |archive-date=7 July 2009}}</ref> It was widely reported in the Spanish media that McManaman's commitment to the team won the respect of his fellow professionals such as Zidane, [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], [[Guti]], [[Iván Helguera]] and the two men often considered to be his two best friends at the club, Figo and Ronaldo, who backed him publicly on several occasions in press interviews.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2007 |title=Ronaldo – One-On-One – Interviews |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/interviews/one-on-one/167/article.aspx |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

Additionally, it is believed that McManaman also forced himself to reinvent his game and transform himself with a versatility that enabled him to play utility roles in the side, thus helping him shake off a nickname he was initially given by the Spanish press, ''El Cartero'' ("the postman"), which suggested that his delivery was unpredictable.<ref>{{Cite news |title='Postman' McManaman delivers on Real promise |work=Independent.ie |url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/postman-mcmanaman-delivers-on-real-promise-26028352.html}}</ref> It was widely regarded as a credit to McManaman that he managed to constantly reinvent himself to be effective and useful in a squad that was widely regarded at the time as the "best team in the world" under the ''Galácticos'' policy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2015 |title=The greatest teams of all time: Madrid 1998-2002 - UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d7ff5471829-4186ad6147f5-1000--the-greatest-teams-of-all-time-madrid-1998-2002/ |access-date=11 March 2019 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Rookwood |first=Dan |title=Macca's staying power |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/oct/23/sport.danrookwood |access-date=11 March 2019}}</ref>

According to certain critics in the Spanish press, McManaman and several other teammates became "victims" as the Real Madrid's ''Galácticos'' policy was often said to be based more on marketing and revenue generation. This sometimes meant players were arguably picked not according to form, but instead owing to their money-making potential off the pitch. McManaman never spoke ill of the ''Galácticos'' policy's effects on him during his tenure, only critiquing the policy and ultimately describing it in his [[autobiography]] ''El Macca'' in 2004 as the "[[Disneyfication]] of Real Madrid" upon his departure from the club.

==Post-playing career==
===Post-retirement football career===
====Managerial and directorial intentions====
In January 2009, McManaman gave a press interview where he stated his intention to go into management. "I'm still thinking of getting back into the game and hopefully I will do my coaching badges at some point this year ... It is going to be hard, though. There seems to be far less jobs available for the younger guys. [[Paul Ince]], [[Roy Keane]], [[Tony Adams]] — it seems as if people have got it in for them. It's becoming a bit less attractive ... If I do get back in, I don't want to be a coach ... I want to be a manager, but that's easier said than done ... I want to be able to pick the team, make the decisions and everything that goes with it. That said, I can't do anything without my badges", he told the ''[[Liverpool Echo]]''.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Setanta's Steve McManaman willing Liverpool to title glory |work=Liverpool Echo |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/setantas-steve-mcmanaman-willing-liverpool-3461863 |access-date=12 July 2014}}</ref>

Reserves and Academy|Liverpool at the academy]] to help nurture the club's future talents.
