McManaman first got a taste for media work in 2005 after he became active as a freelance media [[sports commentator|commentator]] and pundit, providing analysis to [[ITV (TV channel)|ITV]] for the [[2005 UEFA Champions League final]], in which he provided the analysis as his old club Liverpool won the trophy. McManaman then went on to take up opportunities for Asia's largest football broadcasters, [[ESPN Star]] (now Fox Sports Asia), in Singapore in 2006, where he worked alongside commentator [[John Dykes]] and ex-players such as fellow ex-Liverpool star [[Steve McMahon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pearce |first=James |date=9 March 2007 |title=Liverpool F.C. – News – Opportunity knocks for Reds in Asia |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/03/09/opportunity-knocks-for-reds-in-asia-100252-18728585/ |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=Liverpool Echo}}</ref>

By 2007, McManaman became a full-time media pundit, having joined [[Setanta Sports]] as a football [[Color commentator|analyst]] and, for the 2007–08 season, he was given his own television show — ''Macca's Monday Night'' — reflecting on life in the Barclays Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=When Saturday Comes – Beckham and Lovejoy on MLS |url=http://www.wsc.co.uk/content/view/324/29/ |access-date=16 August 2011 |publisher=Wsc.co.uk}}</ref> He hosted the show and was joined by [[Neil Warnock]], [[James Richardson (television presenter)|James Richardson]], [[Emmanuel Petit]], [[Tim Sherwood]], and [[Les Ferdinand]]. The show was finally cancelled in favour of ''Football Matters'', a live late-Monday-night discussion show hosted by Richardson and [[Rebecca Lowe]]. Renowned for his direct comments, in one of McManaman's broadcasts in February 2008, McManaman found himself criticised in the Liverpool press and by former Liverpool fans when his comments for Setanta after a Merseyside derby, on the ownership issue concerning debt involving [[Tom Hicks]] and [[George N. Gillett Jr.|George Gillett]] at [[Anfield]] went down poorly with the supporters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barrett |first=Tony |date=9 February 2008 |title=Steve McManaman attack on fans totally out of order |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2008/02/09/steve-mcmanaman-attack-on-fans-totally-out-of-order-100252-20454242/ |access-date=6 July 2011 |website=Liverpool Echo}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=tabloid|date=February 2026}}

Since July 2010, having joined commentator [[Ian Darke]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nwulu |first=Mac |date=3 November 2010 |title=Steve McManaman Joins ESPN as Soccer Analyst |url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/press-releases/2010/11/steve-mcmanaman-joins-espn-as-soccer-analyst/ |access-date=30 June 2023 |website=ESPN Press Room U.S. |language=en-US}}</ref> and former Germany coach [[Jürgen Klinsmann]], as well as Dutch international [[Ruud Gullit]], on the [[ESPN]] coverage team as a studio analyst for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], he then signed on with the network to be a color commentator for [[Major League Soccer]] and the [[MLS Cup 2010]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2010 |title=MLS Cup 2010 on ESPN HD, ESPN3.com and ESPN Mobile TV |url=http://espnmediazone.com/us/press-releases/2010/11/mls-cup-2010-on-espn-hd-espn3-com-and-espn-mobile-tv/ |access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref> the Premier League, the [[UEFA Euro 2012]],<ref name=":0" /> the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]], and [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], and [[UEFA Euro 2016]], pairing with Darke for all of them.

In late November 2010 and in May 2011, McManaman was the halftime in-studio analyst alongside [[Gary Lineker]] and [[Trevor Francis]] for [[La Liga]]'s ''El Clásico'' broadcast on [[Al Jazeera Sports +3]]. McManaman and Darke were the main ESPN commentary team for [[UEFA Euro 2012]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Nwulu |first=Mac |date=7 June 2012 |title=ESPN Inc. at UEFA EURO 2012 |url=http://espnmediazone.com/us/press-releases/2012/06/espn-inc-at-uefa-euro-2012/ |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=Espnmediazone.com}}</ref> while McManaman was also a guest on daily panel show, ESPN [[PressPass]] (now re-branded as [[ESPN FC]]), alongside [[Steve Nicol]], [[Robbie Mustoe]], [[Shaka Hislop]], [[Robbie Earle]] and [[Gabriele Marcotti]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPN |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/video_audio/138609.html |publisher=ESPN |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921055844/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/video_audio/138609.html |archive-date=21 September 2013}}</ref>

From the 2013–14 season, McManaman joined [[BT Sport]] as one of its lead co-commentators for its new Premier League coverage,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bagchi |first=Rob |date=9 May 2013 |title=Steve McManaman collects campaign medal No3 with BT Sport stint |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/blog/2013/may/09/steve-mcmanaman-bt-sport |website=The Guardian}}</ref> In 2014, McManaman and Darke partnered each other for one last time as co-commentators exclusively for the USA's ESPN coverage of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], in which Darke and McManaman commentated on [[Brazil v Germany (2014 FIFA World Cup)|the match between Brazil and Germany]]; and got plaudits for their incredulous statements, reactions<ref>{{Cite web |title=Germany is Pummeling Brazil in Its Own World Cup, And It Hurts to Watch |url=https://www.bustle.com/articles/30898-germany-is-pummeling-brazil-in-its-own-world-cup-and-it-hurts-to-watch |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=Bustle.com|date=8 July 2014 }}</ref> and colourful comments during the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 December 2014 |title=An eyewitness account: Brazil's humiliation, Germany's World Cup |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/blog/name/68/post/2216252/headline |publisher=ESPN |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref>

From the 2014–15 season onward, McManaman then returned home to be permanently based in England and also could be regularly seen as a guest on BT Sport's Champions League coverage, and on shows like ''Premier League Tonight'' with [[Jake Humphrey]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League Tonight |url=https://sport.bt.com/premier-league-tonight-01364097480603 |website=Sport.bt.com}}</ref> In 2016, McManaman served as a co-commentator for [[UEFA Euro 2016]] on ESPN, alongside Darke for England games as well as a pundit in the studio. In 2018, McManaman returned to ESPNFC as a pundit for the first time since 2012, and on 29 June became the only pundit to correctly predict 12 out of the last 14 in the knockout stages of the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 July 2018 |title=Steve McMananaman's World Cup predictions prove he's a football genius |url=https://www.shortlist.com/news/steve-mcmanaman-brilliant-world-cup-2018-predictions |website=Shortlist.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Clapp |first=Matt |date=14 July 2018 |title=ESPN's Steve McManaman was incredibly accurate in his knockout round World Cup picks |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/espn/espns-steve-mcmanaman-was-incredibly-accurate-in-his-knockout-round-world-cup-picks.html |website=Awfulannouncing.com}}</ref> including getting the semi-finals, final, and ultimate winner exactly correct.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rawson |first=Dov |date=13 July 2018 |title=Steve McManaman shared his World Cup knockout predictions after the group stage |url=https://www.givemesport.com/1352584-steve-mcmanaman-shared-his-world-cup-knockout-predictions-after-the-group-stage |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=GiveMeSport}}</ref> He worked [[UEFA Euro 2020]] in the studio for ESPN mostly alongside [[Alessandro Del Piero]], [[Craig Burley]] and [[Rece Davis]]. ====Dealings with Hong Kong====
In July 2007, McManaman was named [[executive director]] of [[Carson Yeung]]'s [[Hong Kong]]-[[listed company]] Grandtop International Holdings Ltd, which subsequently took a 29.9% stake in Premier League side [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]]. In August 2009, Yeung confirmed that once his proposed takeover of Birmingham City went through, a role at [[St Andrew's (stadium)|St Andrew's]] would be given to McManaman, although he did not specify what role that would be.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 August 2009 |title=Carson Yeung Promises To Spend £5 Million On Players For Birmingham City |url=http://goal.com/en/news/9/england/2009/08/24/1459167/carson-yeung-promises-to-spend-5-million-on-players-for |website=Goal.com |access-date=25 August 2009 |archive-date=27 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090827110428/http://www.goal.com/en/news/9/england/2009/08/24/1459167/carson-yeung-promises-to-spend-5-million-on-players-for |url-status=dead }}</ref> By 2010, McManaman was appointed as a board director at Birmingham City, with fellow director Peter Pannu citing McManaman as being present when some critical board decisions were made—a claim which McManaman denied.<ref name="theguardian.com">{{Cite web |date=27 March 2013 |title=Birmingham City face questions as emails show Peter Pannu's cash demands |url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/mar/27/birmingham-city-peter-pannu |website=The Guardian}}</ref>

On 4 June 2012, it was announced that McManaman had resigned as an executive director of Birmingham International Holdings, the company that owned Birmingham City.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hong Kong Stock Exchange announcement |url=http://202.66.146.82/listco/hk/birminghamint/announcement/a120604.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20160523181157/http%3A//202.66.146.82/listco/hk/birminghamint/announcement/a120604.pdf |archive-date=23 May 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Yeung told to hand over Peak house - the Standard |url=http://www.thestandard.com.hk/news_detail.asp?we_cat%3D4%26art_id%3D123121%26sid%3D36615064%26con_type%3D1%26d_str%3D20120605%26fc%3D2 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140430030713/http://www.thestandard.com.hk/news_detail.asp?we_cat=4&art_id=123121&sid=36615064&con_type=1&d_str=20120605&fc=2 |archive-date=30 April 2014 |access-date=22 September 2012}}</ref> On 19 September 2012, the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]] criticised McManaman "... for failing to use best endeavours to procure Birmingham City International Holdings' compliance with the Exchange Listing Rules".<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 September 2012 |title=The Listing Committee of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited censures the following parties for breaching the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited |url=http://www.hkex.com.hk/eng/newsconsul/hkexnews/2012/120919news.htm |access-date=20 September 2012 |publisher=hkex.com.hk}}</ref> The exchange said the company failed to disclose a large deposit it had to make as it was preparing to buy the English football club Birmingham City in 2009. The exchange also said the purchase of the club should have been put to the company's shareholders for their approval, which it was not. By 2014, Yeung was convicted of [[money laundering]] and Birmingham International was alleged to have been running out of money, leading to its suspension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 December 2014 |title=Hong Kong trading in Birmingham City holdings company suspended after online tirade by director |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/article/1655744/hong-kong-trading-birmingham-city-holdings-company-suspended-after |website=South China Morning Post}}</ref> McManaman maintained throughout that 'he had agreed to be on the board of BIHL for a role which was "more of a PR exercise". He said he had no involvement in any financial dealings, and "stepped away" after June 2011 when Yeung was arrested in Hong Kong and charged with money laundering offences.'<ref name="theguardian.com" />

In 2007–08, McManaman also got involved with corporate dealings in Hong Kong with companies like Sure Trace Inc, which was set up by another [[porn]] baron and [[stock market]] and IT entrepreneur, James MacKay, who transferred two-thirds of the company to him.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 January 2007 |title=ERG's $26m deal with porn boss |work=The Australian |url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/technology/ergs-26m-deal-with-porn-boss/story-e6frgaox-1111112788476?nk=0b03e07d6597331b130e70148fae3cfd |access-date=12 July 2014}}</ref> The company made news for wrong reasons as Sure Trace had made several major contract announcements which had not become actual, revenue-generating contracts and was delisted by the US [[Securities and Exchange Commission]] (SEC). The company then set up True Product ID as a company to conduct technology joint ventures in China and the company was transferred to McManaman. To protect investors, the SEC suspended Sure Trace Security in August 2005, citing the accuracy of public information regarding its technology sales.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 January 2007 |title=ERG tight-lipped on $26m smartcard deal with porn site boss |work=The Australian |url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/erg-tight-lipped-on-26m-smartcard-deal-with-porn-site-boss/story-e6frg8zx-1111112788464?nk=09e86ca1c1a815b006d47900ecd548cc |access-date=12 July 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McManaman's grandfather was a [[bookmaker]] and his father David (in the printing and publishing business,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fremantle |first=Eddie |date=10 March 2002 |title=Footballers' dads |work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2002/mar/10/horseracing.football |access-date=23 September 2024}}</ref> and who played football for [[Pwllheli_F.C.|Pwllheli]] in [[Wales]]) described the family as having "[[horseracing]] in their blood".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fremantle |first=Eddie |date=10 March 2002 |title=Footballers' dads |work=The Observer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2002/mar/10/horseracing.football |access-date=6 July 2011}}</ref> From November 2019, McManaman began writing an exclusive bi-monthly op-ed column for British Horse Racing website, Horseracing.net.<ref>{{Cite web |title=| Horse Racing Journalist |url=https://www.horseracing.net/authors/steve-mcmanaman%22 |website=HorseRacing.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2019 |title=Liverpool legend Steve McManaman's Exclusive Column |url=https://www.horseracing.net/news/steve-mcmanaman-id-send-altior-to-ascot |website=HorseRacing.net}}</ref>

McManaman married his longtime girlfriend (whom he met in the early 90s), Victoria Edwards, a [[barrister#England and Wales|barrister]] and law lecturer (who taught at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 2018 |title=Victoria McManaman: Una mujer emprendedora - Estilo de Vida de Lujo |url=https://www.helencummins.es/victoria-mcmanaman/ |access-date=25 October 2018 |website=Helencummins.es}}</ref> during her time in Madrid with McManaman), on 6 June 2002, in [[Mallorca]]'s [[Palma Cathedral]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 July 2002 |title=McManaman to tie the knot this saturday |url=https://www.majorcadailybulletin.com/news/local/2002/07/03/5459/mcmanaman-tie-the-knot-this-saturday.html |website=Majorcadailybulletin.com}}</ref> The family divides its time between homes in [[Bay of Palma]], London and [[Cheshire]].<ref name="auto1" /> 

McManaman has also spoken about his [[Roman Catholic]] faith and upbringing, and how Real Madrid sought out the blessing of [[Pope John Paul II]] in 2002, saying: "I am a Catholic and what with all the Spanish, Portuguese and Brazilians, we are predominantly a Catholic team..."<ref>{{Cite news |last=McManaman |first=Steve |date=17 September 2002 |title=Real relies on Divine Intervention |work=The Telegraph UK |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/4778007/Real-relies-on-divine-intervention.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=10 October 2020 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/4778007/Real-relies-on-divine-intervention.html |archive-date=12 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Steven McManaman (born 11 February 1972) is an English former professional footballer who played as a winger. He is one of the most decorated English footballers to have played for a club abroad, with the UEFA website stating in 2012 that "of all England's footballing exports in the modern era, none was as successful as McManaman".
During his nine years at Liverpool, McManaman won the FA Cup and League Cup, while individually, he was the Premier League's top assist provider for the 1995–96 season and was named in the PFA Team of the Year for the 1996–97 season. McManaman moved to Real Madrid in 1999, with the transfer becoming one of the most high-profile Bosman free transfers of all time. Amongst his accomplishments with Madrid, he won La Liga and the UEFA Champions League twice, becoming the first English player to win the latter trophy with a non-English club, and later became the first English player to win it for the second time. An early Galáctico, he won eight trophies and played in 11 cup finals in four years and made the semi-finals of the Champions League in each of his four years at the club. He went on to play two seasons at Manchester City before retiring in 2005.
Since his retirement, McManaman works as a co-commentator on ESPN and TNT Sports (formerly BT Sport)'s football coverage, as well acting as a La Liga ambassador. He previously worked as a football pundit for Setanta Sports.
